description:
When: Saturday, August 24, 2013

Who: Teams of 4: 2 Women + 2 Men

What: A one day event featuring a unique series of intense workouts and athletic tests.

Limited to the first 20 teams to register.
- Cost = $160 for the first 10 teams, $200 for the next 10

Hosted by CrossFit Champaign-Urbana and Chief CrossFit

Heat Assignments for the first three workouts have been posted. Heats will be assigned for the fourth workout based on standings after the third workout. You can view the anticipated schedule here: http://bit.ly/13DKxKO


EVENT MAP: http://bit.ly/1d5U2ps

ATHLETE WAIVER: http://bit.ly/1f3aBio

FAQs

Event Format

The event will comprise of 4 Sessions, each session having one workout and one test. Each team will have an assigned heat time for the workout portion during each session, and they will be free to choose when to perform the test during that session time. (For example, Session 1 may run from 9AM to 11AM, Team XYZ is assigned to the 9:45AM heat, and they must perform the test sometime between 9AM and 11AM.)

Teams will receive points according to their placing in each workout and test, similar to Games style scoring. The winner will be the low overall score at the end of the day.  Workouts will each be worth 15% of the total score.  Tests will each be worth 10% of the total score.

Teams must consist of 2 males and 2 females.

Events


PLEASE read all details and watch the videos below to fully understand the workouts and tests BEFORE the day of the event.  If anything is still unclear, let us know!

Session 1
Workout 1: Clean & Carry Ladder
- Men work together and women work together as two-partner teams
- Men start at 135#, women start at 75#
- Partner A cleans the bar and travels 50' with the bar in the front rack position, drops the bar once past the line
- Partner B cleans the bar and travels back the same 50' with the bar in the front rack and drops the bar once past the starting line
- Partners each add (1) 10# plate to each side (for a total of 20#) and replace the collars
- Repeat the Partner A/B clean & carry pattern, the weight increasing by 20# each time
- If one partner is unable to clean & carry the weight, that partner's score is their last successfully completed load. That partner may make as many attempts as desired at this weight, but the other partner may not progress until the failing partner "taps out".
- The other partner may continue completing both legs of the clean & carry until they are also unable to clean & carry the weight, and again this partner's score is their last successfully completed load.
- Partners will have 4 minutes to climb the ladder as high as they can go.
- Workout results will be the sum of the 4 individual clean & carry scores
- Video: http://youtu.be/LfAxkO_TxOY

Test 1: Handstand Walk
- Markers will be taped out at 1' intervals from 0' to 25'
- One at a time, each team member will walk on their hands for max distance
- To start, both hands must be stationary on the ground behind the 0' mark with both feet in the air
- The score will be the last 1' interval with both hands across while both feet are still in the air
- At the 25' mark there will be a cone which athletes that complete the 25' may go around and come back, still inverted and earn additional footage.  There will be a cone at the 0' mark to again allow athletes to go around and continue racking up footage (if they're crazy good gymnasts and still inverted at this point!)
- Mulligans: each team will have (2) mulligans (do-overs) to use as they wish, but each individual member will log only (1) score. 
- The team score will be the sum of the individual members' footage traversed
- Video: http://youtu.be/L7Sbei8UQ4Q

Session 2
Workout 2: AMRAP & Sled Push
- 2a = 8 Minutes to accumulate as many points as possible as follows
- Teams will start behind a starting line
- Teams will cycle through assigned order of W1, W2, M1, M2
- One teammate at a time will run through a series of 30" hurdles and arrive at a pull-up rig
- Once at the rig the athlete will have the option of performing a max unbroken set of EITHER pull-ups, chest-to-bar pull-ups, or bar muscle-ups.  The athlete must announce to the judge which they will be performing BEFORE getting on the bar.  The athlete may only perform one movement type per trip to the bar (i.e. no changing movements part way through a given set)
- Max unbroken set means no resting at any point in the movement, i.e. no hanging still from the bar, no resting at the top of a muscle-up
- Pull-ups = 1pt each, CTB Pull-ups = 2pts each, Bar MUs = 5pts each
- Once the athlete drops from the bar, they will run through the same series of hurdles back to the start line and tag the next athlete in the sequence on their team.
- Teams will continue the cycle until time is called.
- Once time is called there will be a (1) minute rest period followed immediately by...
- 2b = 90-second Sled Push for Distance
- Sleds will start loaded with 90# at the 0 marker
- Teams will cycle through the same assigned order as in 2a, again starting with W1
- Each athlete will push the sled (1) interval of approximately 15' (each interval will be marked with a line that the sled must fully cross) and then leave the sled and sprint back to tag the next teammate in the sequence at the start line
- The first (4) intervals will be worth 5pts each.
- At the 4th interval line there will be (2) 45" plates which will need to be added to the sled before it is pushed further
- Intervals 5 through 8 will be worth 10pts each
- Thus, teams have an opportunity to earn 60pts in the sled push
- If any athlete is unable to push the sled, they must at least run to the sled, touch it and return to tag the next athlete in the sequence.
- The team's total score will be the sum of points earned in 2a + 2b
- Video: http://youtu.be/CANXGU6QmmU

Test 2: Max Height Vertical Jump
- A vertical jump test aparatus will be set up to test each athlete for the total elevation difference between their maximum reach standing flat-footed and their maximum jumping reach
- Each athlete will log (1) score
- Mulligans: each team will have (2) mulligans (do-overs) to use as they wish, but each individual member will log only (1) score. 
- The team score will be the sum of all (4) athlete's logged scores
- Video: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X-i_2U5OdtA

Session 3
Workout 3: Mini-Oly Meet
- Teams will have 20 minutes to log a max snatch and a max clean & jerk score per athlete
- All athletes on a team must log a score for the snatch before moving on to the clean & jerks
- Teams will each have a women's bar with assorted weights and a men's bar with assorted weights and enough room for two athletes to be lifting
- Only one athlete may perform a scoring lift at a time under the watch of their assigned judge
- Athletes MUST verify the load on the bar with the judge BEFORE making a scoring attempt
- The team's score will be the sum of all (8) loads (1 snatch and 1 c&j per athlete)
- Video: http://youtu.be/eP6iFVYcDNI

Test 3: 40-yd dash
- A 40-yd dash testing aparatus will be set up to time each athlete's sprinting ability
- Each athlete will log (1) score.
- Mulligans: each team will have (2) mulligans (do-overs) to use as they wish, but each individual member will log only (1) score. 
- The team score will be the sum of all (4) athlete's logged scores.  In this event, the lowest total time wins.
- Video: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PsCTJnaHke8

Session 4: To be announced the day of the event!

Don't worry about it.  Sign up with as complete a team as you can.  Just make sure you have your team together at least 1 week before the competition.

 

Do I have to bring my printed ticket to the event?

This fun and informal workshop is a great chance to learn new cooking techniques and recipes to bring out the best in seasonal produce.

The day starts with gathering our ingredients as we harvest produce from the vegetable garden, milk a cow or two (depending on the season), collect the eggs and have a good chat with the pigs before we head back to the big open kitchen to start cooking.  Cooking is hands on and shared as we prepare a three course feast - the menu changes from session to session to reflect the changing availability of seasonal produce through the year. 

Recent menus:

Handmade ravioli with spinach and ricotta made with milk from the house cow, coq au vin using farm roosters and pumpkin pie with preserved apricots.

Handmade chestnut pasta with rosemary and walnuts, hot smoked farm pork with garden salads and tart tartin using wild apples.

The afternoon is all about enjoying the fruits of our labours as we settle in to enjoy our meal and a glass or two of local wine.

8 places only per session.

 ----------

Eye and Leaf is set on a pretty 113 acre working farm in Gippsland Victoria, an easy 90 minute drive from Melbourne.  An abundance of food is produced on the farm including eggs, dairy, poultry, beef, pork, fruit, berries and vegetables making Eye and Leaf almost completely self sufficient. 

The focus is on producing delicious food using ethical and sustainable practices and the results are inspiring for anyone interested in more sustainable use of resources or growing their own. 

You can read more about Eye and Leaf here.

description:
Learn the foundations Bayesian Networks and how to use them as a practical research framework with the BayesiaLab software platform. Join us for this 3-day course, July 9-11, 2013 in Chicago, IL.

Audience: Applied researchers, statisticians, data scientists, data miners, epidemiologists, predictive modelers, econometricians, economists, market researchers, knowledge managers, marketing scientists, students and teachers in related fields.

Level: The course will be taught at a beginner level, so no prior knowledge of Bayesian networks is necessary. However, undergraduate-level familiarity with probability theory and statistics is recommended.

Objective: Completing the course as a Certified BayesiaLab Analyst and becoming proficient in using Bayesian networks for a broad range of applied research and analytics tasks.

Syllabus

Dr. Lionel Jouffe, who is one of the world's foremost experts on Bayesian networks, will host this 3-day seminar and teach his proven curriculum. The course covers the basics of probabilistic graphical models and introduces BayesiaLab as the software platform for manually modeling and machine-learning Bayesian networks. Participants will learn how to generate Bayesian networks for a wide range of analytics tasks, including:

  • prediction/forecasting 
  • diagnostics
  • classification
  • clustering
  • missing values imputation
  • what-if scenario simulation
  • target optimization

Special emphasis will be given to observational versus causal inference, which is particularly relevant in the context of Big Data. Course topics are presented in alternating sessions of lectures and exercises, with ample opportunity for Q&A.

In conjunction with the seminar, participants will have access to an unrestricted 60-day license of BayesiaLab 5.0.7 Professional (the very latest release), so they can experiment with the full array of functions during and after the training.

The class is limited to a maximum of ten participants in order to allow for one-on-one coaching during the hands-on exercises with BayesiaLab. This small-group format provides a productive yet informal learning environment that facilitates a lively dialogue between participants from a wide range of backgrounds (see testimonials).

Terms & Conditions 

  • The tuition fee for the 3-day course for commercial participants is US$ 2,995.
  • Members of government agencies, the military and non-profit organizations are eligible for a reduced tuition fee of US$ 2,245 (≈25% discount).*
  • Student and faculty of accredited academic institutions are eligible for a reduced tuition fee of US$ 1,495 (50% discount).*
  • A 60-day license to the full version of BayesiaLab Professional 5.2 will be provided to all participants for installation on their computers prior to the event.
  • Participants will be required to bring their own WiFi-enabled computer/laptop to the seminar (Windows XP/Vista/7/8 or Mac OS X).
  • The course fee includes all training materials, beverages, lunch and snacks during the training.
  • Accommodation is at the participants' own expense.

*Proof of affiliation will be required upon registration. If you are not sure about your eligibility for reduced tuition fees, please email us at info@bayesia.us.

Testimonials from Earlier Courses

"A must-take course for anyone looking to leverage advanced BBN techniques in virtually any domain." - Alex Cosmas, Booz Allen Hamilton

"Attend, attend, attend! The training was well done allowing for both hands-on using BayesiaLab but also exploration of the Bayesian approach. Lionel was a great teacher – to have the brain behind the product guiding you was indeed amazing, no question went unanswered." - Yianna Vovides, The George Washington University

"Bayesian Belief Networks is an advanced technique and Bayesia Lab makes such a complex technique easy to use on fingertips. Without any prior knowledge I had attended the Bayesia Lab Training in Chicago, April 2011 and found it very helpful & worth the money paid. The course structure / contents were well planned and by the end of the course I felt satisfied & had sense of mission accomplished.  Dr. Jouffe has excellent teaching skills & in his training session there were several Q&A opportunities all addressed with a smiling face." - Senior Scientist at Fortune 500 CPG company

"The Bayesia training session was one of the most valuable and thoughtful I have ever attended. Dr. Jouffe did an admirable job introducing and explaining Bayesian Belief Networks, an area of predictive modeling that is of rapidly increasing importance in many fields. The course adroitly mixed practical applications, case histories, and key concepts and theory, explaining the uses and remarkable power of these models. The approach was always informative and engaging, and included the best set of presentation materials I have encountered in a long time. This is a truly worthwhile course, and it also introduced a remarkable piece of analytical software. I speak as somebody who has given seminars and taught graduate courses for over twenty years; this session definitely deserves the highest praise." - Steven Struhl, Principal at SMS Research Analysis

"I enjoyed the training course in Chicago in April 2011. It was very interesting and very well organized. I learned a lot of new things and I got inspired for applications of BayesiaLab in my daily job. Finally the environment: very friendly and productive with the other attendees coming both from business and academic world, a really wonderful “melting pot”. A very exiting experience which I recommend to all people interested in Bayesian networks." - Tommaso Pronunzio, Partner at Ales Market Research (Italy), ESOMAR Representative

"I attended this training in Feb 2012 in Orlando. Dr. Jouffe did a great job explaining concepts of Bayesian Belief Networks. The hands-on sessions are extremely interesting. The BayesiaLab software has a lot of functions - you can do anything from correlation analysis to supervised learning algorithms! This tool can be for analysis in any area - ranging from market research to health care. I recommend this training to all people interested in Bayesian networks" - Krithika Bhuvaneshwar, Bioinformatician/Data Manager, Clinical Informatics, Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center, Georgetown University

org_desc:
Bayesia USA is the North American sales and consulting organization for France-based Bayesia S.A.S. Their mission is to promote Bayesian networks as a new framework for knowledge discovery and reasoning within complex domains.

Founded by two professors in the field of artificial intelligence in 2001 and headquartered in northwestern France, Bayesia S.A.S. is the world's leading developer of research software based on the Bayesian network paradigm. Their principal product, BayesiaLab, is the only software platform that can perform unsupervised structural learning for knowledge discovery.

Today, BayesiaLab is being used by researchers in major organizations around the world, including P&G, Unilever, BBDO, GroupM, GfK, TNS, Ipsos, Mu Sigma, Booz Allen Hamilton, InterContinental Hotels Group, Dell and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory among many others.

description:
Please join the Glendower Parent Community in viewing Miss Representation, a documentary which explores how the media’s misrepresentations of women have led to the underrepresentation of women in positions of power and influence.

Monday 17th June, 2013 - Drinks will be served at 7:30pm and the screening will start at 8:15pm.  A panel discussion will follow the screening and end at 10:30pm.

Like drawing back a curtain to let bright light stream in, Miss Representation uncovers a glaring reality we live with every day but fail to see. Written and directed by Jennifer Siebel Newsom, the film exposes how mainstream media contribute to the under-representation of women in positions of power and influence in America. The film challenges the media’s limited and often disparaging portrayals of women and girls, which make it difficult for women to achieve leadership positions and for the average woman to feel powerful herself.

While women have made great strides in leadership over the past few decades, our society where media is the most persuasive force shaping cultural norms, the collective message that our young women and men overwhelmingly receive is that a woman’s value and power lie in her youth, beauty, and sexuality, and not in her capacity as a leader.

Stories from teenage girls and provocative interviews with politicians, journalists, entertainers, activists and academics, like Condoleezza Rice, Nancy Pelosi, Katie Couric, Rachel Maddow, Margaret Cho, Rosario Dawson, Jean Kilbourne and Gloria Steinem build momentum as Miss Representation accumulates startling facts and statistics that will leave the audience shaken and armed with a new perspective.

The documentary premiered at the 2011 Sundance Film Festival.
name: Miss Representation

Monday, June 10th

@The New Parkway Theatre, 474 24thSt. Oakland, CA 94612
doors: 6:15pm
Film: 6:30pm
+ Q & A w/ Filmmakers via Skype
w/ music by Colin Mutchler 

All-Ages | Tix $10 (available online & at the door - if not Sold-Out)

Community Partners: Occupy Oakland, Earth Tribe Yoga, Louder 

Occupy Love explores the growing realization that the dominant system of power is failing to provide us with health, happiness or meaning.   The old paradigm that concentrates wealth, founded on the greed of the few, is causing economic and ecological collapse. The resulting crisis has become the catalyst for a profound awakening:  millions of people are deciding that enough is enough –  the time has come to create a new world, a world that works for all life.

The film connects the dots in this era of rapidly evolving social change, featuring captivating insider scenes from the Egyptian Revolution, the Indignado uprising in Spain,  Occupy Wall Street in New York, Indigenous activists at the Alberta Tar Sands, the climate justice movement, and beyond. Woven throughout the action oriented backbone of the film is a deep exploration of public love, and compelling stories of an emerging new paradigm.  It features some of the world’s key visionaries on alternative systems of economics, sustainability, and empathy, including Naomi Klein, Bill McKibben, Jeremy Rifkin, bell hooks and Charles Eisenstein.

Occupy Love is directed by VELCROW RIPPER. Produced by NOVA AMI, IAN MACKENZIE and VELCROW RIPPER.

description:
“A sober and quiet mind is one in which the ego does not obstruct the fluency of things that come in through our senses and up through our dreams.  Our business in living is to become fluent with the life we are living, and art can help this.”     John Cage
 
Artistic pursuits involve a hunt for freedom in the inner workings of the mind.  Mindfulness, as taught by the Buddha, is a means of attending to one’s inner environment in a disciplined way.  Artists throughout the ages have turned to similar strategies for help in bringing their creative impulses to fruition.  Mindfulness frees the artist from automatic reactivity and brings forth the discovery of an inner space of blissful (if sometimes painful) inspiration.  Compassion drives the hard labor of creativity, drawing energy from its intolerance of suffering and shaping appearances in such a way that people are lifted, however slightly, into a deeper and vaster sensitivity.
 
Today’s workshop aims to make both mindfulness and compassion available in a meaningful and accessible way to its participants.  Through both discussion and practice we will strive to meet the challenge laid out by the great master John Cage: to become fluent with the life we are living. 

Saturday, June 1; 10AM-5PM

Mark Epstein, MD is a psychiatrist in NewYork City and the author of books about the interface of Buddhism and psychotherapy. He is currently Clinical Assistant Professor in the Postdoctoral Program in Psychotherapy and Psychoanalysis at New York University.

Sharon Salzberg is cofounder of the Insight Meditation Society (IMS) in Barre, Massachusetts. She is one of America's leading meditation teachers and authors. For more information about Sharon, please visit: www.SharonSalzberg.com.

Velez as Quintessence Consultants LLC, which focused on consulting for various entities in their security and loss prevention needs.  As time progressed, Amilkar noticed there was a void that existed in the delivery of quality security and investigative services.

Focusing on the 3E’s approach to problem solving (Enforcement, Engineering, and Education), the company evolved into Blackjacket Security.  Blackjacket Security offered unparalleled delivery of security services in both armed and unarmed capacities, investigative services and training programs in the security, investigative and emergency services field.

The company continued to grow and in 2013 it once again evolved into what is known as Blackjacket Group. Teaching under the guidelines of the American Heart Association, ASP, SABRE, the New Jersey Safety Council and the New Jersey 

State Police, our course offerings include SORA classes (Security Officer Registration Act), ACLS, PALS, BLS for the Healthcare Provider CPR, Heartsaver CPR and Heartsaver First Aid.  We also offer Defensive Driving, Pepper Spray Defense, Tactical Baton and Tactical Handcuffing.

The company is an authorized dealer of Caridac Science and Philips Automated External Defibrillators (AED's).  Blackjacket Group also runs an e-store selling safety and security related products.

2013 SUMMIT on COLLEGE SUCCESS

The academic, financial, and socio-cultural challenges facing low-income high school students in their transition to and through college remain formidable and well documented.  In keeping with its mission to overcome these obstacles, the Cristo Rey Network launched the University Partner Initiative in 2009 to formalize strategic relationships with colleges and universities committed to expanding its capacity and furthering its mission to “transform urban America, one student at a time” in new, mutually beneficial ways.  The initiative seeks to identify, inform, and promote new instituonal supports and programs that ensure college success for Cristo Rey and other low-income students across the country.  We are deeply grateful to our 24 National and 22 Supporting Partners who help us realize our mission. 

As part of our ongoing commitment to sharing what we are learning with our schools and partners, Cristo Rey hosts an annual Summit to showcase promising research, programs, and practices that have enhanced college success for Cristo Rey Network students and alumni.   Please consider joining us for this 2-day conversation that will include Cristo Rey high schools, university partners, researchers, and thought partners from the field.   

Travel + Hotel Information
Click here for detailed instructions regarding travel to/from campus.  A block of discounted rooms ($116/night) have been reserved for Summit participants at The Hilton Garden Inn in Worcester to help reduce costs.    Rooms will be released at the end of June so be sure to reserve yours today by calling the hotel (508-753-5700) and requesting the Cristo Rey Summit rate.   For all those flying, Boston's Logan International Airport and Providence's T.F. Green Airport are both an easy 1 hour drive from campus.  
 
Agenda
July 23: Pre-Summit workshops and sessions for Cristo Rey schools, Visit to Cristo Rey Boston High School, National Partner Welcome Reception 
July 24 & 25: Opening Mass, Breakout sessions, Partner Recognition Dinner, Keynote, Networking Fair, and more

Participants
Participants have included a diverse group of senior university leaders from enrollment, financial aid, and student affairs in addition to Cristo Rey school presidents, college counselors, alumni advisors, and alumni ambassadors.   Below is a list of organizations that have participated in the past.

How do the choices we make to satisfy our basic needs impact the health of our community and our environment? Find out all summer long in an open-forum to explore and discuss critical topics with cutting-edge thinkers.

Fritz Haeg's inspiring work around the world includes edible gardens, public dances, educational environments, animal architecture, domestic gatherings, urban parades, temporary encampments, documentary videos, publications, exhibitions, websites, and occasionally buildings for people. Recent projects include Edible Estates – an international series of public domestic edible gardens; Animal Estates – a housing initiative for native wildlife in cities around the world which debuted at the 2008 Whitney Biennial; Sundown Schoolhouse – an itinerant educational program, which evolved out of the Sundown Salon gatherings at his geodesic home base in the hills of Los Angeles; the designs, encampments, and scores of Fritz Haeg Studio; and starting in 2012, the new traveling project series of Domestic Integrities.

Haeg studied architecture in Italy at the Istituto Universitario di Architettura di Venezia and Carnegie Mellon University, where he received his B. Arch. He is a Rome Prize fellow – in residence at the American Academy in Rome from 2010-2011, a MacDowell Colony Fellow (2007, 2009 and 2010), Montalvo Arts Center fellow (2012), and nominated for National Design Awards in 2009 and 2010. He has variously taught in architecture, design, and fine art programs at Princeton University (2012), California Institute of the Arts (CalArts), Art Center College of Design, Parsons School of Design, the University of Southern California, and Wayne State University in Detroit as the Elaine L. Jacob Chair in Visual Art visiting professor for Fall 2012.

Haeg has produced and exhibited projects at MoMA; Tate Modern; the Walker Art Center; the Hayward Gallery, London; the Liverpool Biennial; Blood Mountain Foundation, Budapest; the Whitney Museum of American Art; The Guggenheim Museum; SALT Beyo?lu, Istanbul; Stroom, Den Haag; Arup Phase 2, London; Pollinaria, Abruzzo; San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; Casco Office of Art, Design and Theory, Utrecht; Mass MoCA; the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia; the Wattis Institute, San Francisco; the Netherlands Architecture Institute; The Indianapolis Museum of Art; and the MAK Center, Los Angeles; The Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum; and the Center for Advanced Visual Studies at MIT among other institutions. His work has been published internationally, including profiles and features in The New York Times, Financial Times, Frieze, Artforum, The Independent, Dwell, Men’s Vogue, BBC, NPR, ABC World News Tonight, CBS Evening News, and The Martha Stewart Show. Recent books include “The Sundown Salon Unfolding Archive” (Evil Twin Publications, 2009), “Edible Estates: Attack on the Front Lawn” (Metropolis Books, 2008. 3rd ed. 2013), and “Rome Eats Rome” (NERO, expected Fall 2013).

 

Learn how you can become a member to get special rates on lectures and workshops thruought the year!


Cancellation Policy:

We understand your plans may change. With that in mind, The Ecology Center has a very simple cancellation policy: regardless of whether you made your reservation online or by phone, we will give you credit toward a future program if you cancel at least 24 hours ahead of an event. Credit must be redeemed within 90 days of issue.

Unfortunately, as a small non-profit, we cannot give refunds or credits if cancelled with less than 24-hours notice or in the event of a no-show. This policy is in effect for all events and classes, except for Green Feast; due to high demand, no refunds or credits will be issued for our annual fundraising event.

Sobe House of Fab Presents A Monthly High Fashion SHOP, SWAP, And SELL Event EVERY 2nd Saturday At Lincoln Rd. Mall On The Corner Of Dylan's Candy Bar Located At 801 Lincoln Rd  Miami Beach, FL 33139. 



Be good. Be green. Be Glam!

Relax, mingle, get pampered and SWAP (exchange or sell) clothes, shoes and accessories you no longer need or wear.
Clothing Swaps are revolutionizing America's approach to fashion. SWAP ~ SELL ~ SHOP ~ SAVE at Sobe House of Fab Swap In The City Events! $$$ Buy Tickets NOW at

 

 *First 50 people who register online get a FREE swag bag!*

 

FAQs:

1. What can I bring to swap or to sell? 

Bring designer tops, bottoms, dresses, jackets, shoes, handbags and accessories. The items have to be current and fashionable. We will accept vintage items if we feel it is swap-able. Items should be in good to new condition, with working zippers and no missing buttons. Items should be clean. We will not accept any items with holes, stains, or pilling. Items from ALL seasons are welcome.


 

2. What designer brands do you accept?

Bring in designer brands such as:  BCBG, Coach, Joie, Splendid, Elizabeth & James, Ella Moss, Theory, Marc Jacobs, Micheal Kors, 3.1 Phillip Lim, Rag & Bone, Seven of Mankind, Joe’s, Milly, Missoni, Nanette Lepore, Rebecca Minkoff, Pour la Victoire, Tumi, Valentino, etc.

If it’s a brand found at Macy's, Saks, Nordstrom or Bloomies, bring it to the party!  We will also accept on-style brands such as Zara, Aldo, Forever21, H&M, Gap, Old Navy, Air Jordans, Brooks Brothers, Polo, Izod, Penguin, Club Monaco, JCrew, Banana Republic, MANGO, Guess, Anthropologie, and designer collaborations like Jimmy Choo or Versace for H&M, Alexander Wang for Target & Neimans, etc. Of course super designer brands are also welcome like Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Chanel, etc. 


3. What should I NOT bring?

Gym wear (sweats, sports bras, etc), hair accessories, bathing suits, and undergarments are not accepted, unless the tags are still on.

Fakes will strongly discouraged!  We will do our best to authenticate but we cannot guarantee the authenticity of an item.

Golden rule of swapping is swap items that you would be proud to give to your best friend. 

 

4.  Do I have to bring swap items to come to the party?

No, please rsvp and come join the party for fun!

 

5. How does the swap work?

Here's an easy step-by-step process: 

1) Go through your closet and find stylish clothes, shoes, and accessories you no longer wear. Shoes, purses (bags), belts, hats, and men's clothing? Sure! But please only five accessories per person.Please coordinate your pieces on a hanger into a fabulous fashion forward ready-to-wear outfit.   ALL clothing will be swapped as a completed outfit or ensemble only!!! On every item the brand and size tags must be legible. Leave your old washed-out clothing at home. We only want the best!

2) Not too much and not too little: bring at least three but no more than eight carefully selected pieces of clothing for the Swap-Boutique. Bring only beautiful things: we want to maintain a fabulous selection of high quality clothing for you to choose from. Bring us your clothing in the same condition that you would lend them to your BFF: freshly washed and folded, and if possible, ironed as well! Calling all models, stylists, fashion + jewelry+ accessory designers, and thrift+ consignment boutiques...This is YOUR TIME TO SHINE!!!

3) Guest are able to SWAP or SELL their own items as well as shop the closets of the featured Guest celebrities

3) Drop off your items from 8:30-10:00 AM. We will stamp your hand and will give you tickets that coincide with the pieces you brought in. 

We will have a color coding system in place to keep swapping equal and fair:

RED = Up to $100

WHITE = Up to $300

YELLOW = Up to $500

BLUE = $500 +

4) Swap begins at 8:30am. Remember, swapping is not a contact sport!  Swaps are fun and a great way to meet like-minded people, so please be nice to fellow swappers.

5) Enjoy your fabulous, new-to-you wardrobe!

 

6. Can I try on my clothes? If so, where?

There won't be an area where you can try on clothes, but you can certainly try them on over your clothes, or have a couple of your girlfriends cover you up!

Is there an age limit to enter the event?

This is just for boys & girls aged 7 to 11 years old

 

Do I need loads of acting experience?

If you have lots of experience that's great! but you don't need it.

 

How many other children will be there?

There'll be no more than 18 children plus two actors who will be running the event.

The fun begins from the moment you arrive. Can I pay on the door?

Possibly, but to guarantee a place you need to book in advance

 

What are my parking options getting to the event?

There is a small car park useful for dropping participants off.

 

What can/can't I bring to the event?

Most important of all - Please bring a packed lunch !! and wear comfortable clothes - if you'd really like to get nto the spirit of it all then why not wear 1940's clothing!

 

Where can I contact the organiser with any questions?

You can contact me, Paul Wilkinson at kingfisherpost@gmail.com

 

Is my registration/ticket transferrable?

Yes, if you can't make it then by all means pass the ticket to someone else (so long as they are the right age!)

 

Do I have to bring my printed ticket to the event?

Yes please! - If you lose it before the day, please bring proof of purchase with you and we'll do what we can to make sure you get in.

 

What is the refund policy?

If the event is cancelled by us, we will refund your ticket fee. If you are unable to attend for your own reasons then we are unable to refund your ticket fee, but you are welcome to pass it on or sell it to someone else (we'd prefer you to charge them cost price please!)

description:
Bright Business Tour - Manchester


The Bright Business Tour was conceived on a rainy afternoon in early May. After a lengthy discussion about what types of business seminars are available we decided to run a survey and ask people what they wanted. A few days later we had received hundreds of responses from businesses across the UK telling us what they looked for in a seminar.

So far the survey respondents have decided the following:

  • Where the seminars are
  • How long they should be
  • The subjects of the seminars
  • How much the tickets cost.

That is not the end of your involvement in the seminar!

When you buy a ticket you will be allowed to submit your question or request to Robert. In each session Robert will answer these questions and queries as part of the seminar content.


Morning Session - Bright Strategy and Money
Where are you going, how are you going to get there and how much are you going to make?

A boring title but totally crucial! Too many businesses create lame strategies (if they have one in the first place) so it is little wonder that they also deliver lame results. While this is not a ‘get-rich-quick’ programme it will cover the basics of how to put together a strategic plan that actually delivers for your business. We then go on to talk about pricing and cash and the implications of getting it wrong right. You will be taken through a masterclass in how to design, set up and deliver a profitable strategy for you and your business.

Afternoon Session - Bright Marketing and Selling
How to attract the right customer and get them to buy from you (so you make a profit).

Most people feel that their marketing just isn’t delivering the promised results. It is easy to sell ‘loads of stuff’, just give it away for free! However, what is clever is to sell the right product to the right people and at the right price. Everyone wants to know the ‘secrets of…’ but actually the marketing fundamentals are pretty straightforward. You will be taken through a step-by-step process to significantly improve your sales.

 


Testimonials from the Bristol and London seminars:

 

“Refreshing stimulus to review my business’s future”

“It was all hugely useful – thank you!”

“I would recommend these courses to others"

description:
“Action, drama, torture, and even heroism.”

Logging miles and investigating the most quotidian details, Jørgen Leth's A SUNDAY IN HELL tenderly investigates the potent cocktail of culture and humanity that add up to a bicycling championship.

The subject is the legendary Paris-Roubaix race, and Leth’s production deploys a small army’s worth of camera positions. Whether you wear one of those silly-looking biker caps every day or you've never gripped a pair of handlebars in your life, you'll be pulverized by the cinematography: regularly zooming in on individual participants from parallel cars, bikes and helicopters, the camera tracks rivers of bikes as they bend along sunny curves and the race guts entire towns, trickling out into the countryside.

The relationship between camera and subject make for a grueling, classic documentary that feels closer to live dance; the dust-caked faces of the agog spectators will match your own.

"You can see every bead of sweat on the cyclists and every smashed-up ankle. It really makes you never want to get on a bike again. But it is an amazing film." - Nick Fraser, BBC

"Arguably the best film ever made about professional cycling." - Peter Cowie, International Film Guide


Duration: 111 mins
Nationality: Danish
Year: 1977
Directed By: Jørgen Leth
Produced By: Jørgen Leth

The cinema is the lovely Moorland Discovery Centre in the woods at Longshaw Estate very close to the Fox House Pub, some 5 miles outside of Sheffield on the border between Derbyshire and South Yorkshire. The wooden building, insulated with sheep's wool in the walls, is cosy, pretty, and kitted out with a decent sound system, projector and screen. It seats around 50 people.

The evenings will start at 8pm giving you time to grab a bite to eat after work and cycle up the hill. You will be able to order tea/ coffee and cake when booking your tickets so don't worry about low blood-sugar. Things will wrap up between 9.30pm and 10pm giving you time to freewheel home and jump in the shower before bed.

...et voila - exercise, entertainment and a social, all in the same evening.

In case you are wondering, yes we will allow you in if you don't come by bike, but we hope you'll enter into the spirit of things.

Environmental Site Assessment in Ontario (ESA) - June 4 and 6, 2013 - 6:00 to 9:00 pm

These talks will provide an introduction to Environmental Site Assessment in Ontario and Ontario Regulation 153/04 (commonly referred to as the “Brownfields Act”). The Brownfields Act is the cornerstone to environmental practice in Ontario and a basic understanding of its contents should be useful to those working in environmental consulting. The talks will outline the contents of the Regulation and review the methods for conducting Environmental Site Assessments in Ontario. The main focus will be on conducting Phase One and Two ESA’s with a brief introduction to Site Remediation and Risk Assessment.

Outline:

Introduction of terms and the components of O.Reg. 153/04

Phase One ESA

Phase Two ESA

Site Remediation

Risk Assessment

Case study

description:
How does your organization maintain it’s competitive edge in a changing economy? And what does this mean for your bottom line?

This workshop outlines strategies that will help your business realize increased profit margins by 51 – 81% over a 3-5 year period as a direct result of investments in organizational sustainability.

Prosperity returns are realized in the following ways:

  • Increased revenue and market share
  • Brand recognition
  • Engaged, productive and committed employees
  • Cost savings on waste, water and energy expenditures from efficiency
  • Cost savings from decreased attrition costs
  • Reduced risks
  • Future market value impact and returns

About the Hosts

Sara Blenkhorn

Enthusiastic, innovative and creative, Sara is a futurist with a talent to think big. She has an extensive history of engaging businesses to create a shared value proposition around sustainability and then bake it into the DNA of their operations resulting in an enhanced bottom line and increased value to their community, stakeholders and shareholders. Holding the belief that businesses are society’s most influential forces for social change, Sara’s vision is to make impact on a colossal scale. Sara holds a Masters degree in Strategic Leadership Towards Sustainability, and has served as an advisor for The Natural Step International. Her experience working with a wide range of organizations all over the world has given her a diverse set of skills and tools to help organizations take the leap from good intentions to long term organizational resiliency.

 

Timothy Nash

Timothy Nash is President of Strategic Sustainable Investments, and teaches economics at Sheridan College. As an expert on socially responsible investing, impact investing, and the green economy, he has been featured in The Globe & Mail, Advisor’s Edge Report, and Reuters, and has appeared on CBC’s The Lang & O’Leary Exchange (video above). He earned a BA in Economics from Dalhousie University (Halifax, Canada) and a Master's in Strategic Leadership towards Sustainability from the Blekinge Institute of Technology (Karlskrona, Sweden).

Timothy is the lead researcher for Ethical Market’s Green Transition Scoreboard® research report, which details more than $4.1 trillion of private investments in the global green economy since 2007.  He lives in Toronto, Canada and is often found cavorting about the Centre for Social Innovation.
name: The Business Case for Sustainability

description:
The Chicago Council of the Navy League of the U.S., in partnership with the Union League Club of Chicago, invites members and their guests to attend a special luncheon with Navy Vice Admiral Bruce E. Grooms, Deputy Chief of Staff for Capability and Development at Supreme Allied Command Transformation.

Vice Admiral Grooms, who will be in Chicago to serve as the commencement speaker for the Hyman G. Rickover Naval Academy’s graduation ceremony, will join us for lunch on June 17 to discuss his responsibilities in his new role and to reflect upon the readiness and operational capabilities of America's Navy.  Prior to his current assignment, Vice Admiral Grooms served as Assistant Deputy Chief of Naval Operations for Plans and Strategy, Office of the Chief of Naval Operations, Pentagon, Washington, D.C. 

A native of Cleveland, OH, VADM Grooms graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy with a Bachelor of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering. Following completion of nuclear power training, he served in nearly every capacity aboard a variety of submarines including a tour as executive officer of USS Pasadena (SSN 752) where he twice deployed to the Persian Gulf. 

His command tours included USS Asheville (SSN 758). During this tour, the ship received the Battle Efficiency "E" award, the Golden Anchor and Silver Anchor for the highest retention in the Submarine Force. He subsequently served as commander, Submarine Squadron Six and later as commander, Submarine Group Two. 

Ashore, he served as a company officer and later as the Commandant of Midshipmen at the United States Naval Academy. He served as the senior military assistant to the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy. He was the vice director, Joint Staff and later served on the chief of naval operations’ staff as the assignment deputy CNO for Operations, Plans and Strategy.

Please join us to welcome Vice Admiral Grooms back to Chicago!  The cost of the luncheon is $30 per person, inclusive of tax and gratuity.
name: Navy League Luncheon with Vice-Admiral Bruce Grooms

description:
Austin Toastmasters 32nd Annual Awards Banquet

with Honoree Major Mary Jennings Hegar



During the past four decades, The Austin Toastmasters Club has had a tradition of honoring an influential Texan with the Communication Achievement Award. To view the list of past local luminary recipients, please see this link: http://austintoastmasters.org/index.php/special-events/annual-communication-award-recipients. Major Mary Jennings Hegar will be the 32nd honoree to receive this prestigious Austin Toastmasters award.

                                           

Major Mary Jennings Hegar served three tours over two deployments to Afghanistan as a Combat Search and Rescue (CSAR) pilot. She was awarded the Purple Heart and the Distinguished Flying Cross with a Valor Device for heroism while participating in an aerial mission near Kandahar Airfield on July 29, 2009. Major Hegar is the sixth woman to receive the DFC, the first being Amelia Earhart, and only the second person in history to receive the DFC with Valor Device. 

Click on the following link to view Major Hegar being interviewed on MSNBC http://video.msnbc.msn.com/msnbc/50039412#50039412

After returning home Major Hegar again made history by becoming the lead plaintiff in Hegar v. Panetta, the ACLU lawsuit challenging and overturning the military’s policy excluding women from combat positions.  Additionally, as the official spokesperson for OurPart.US, Major Hegar is championing crowd funding initiatives to provide ADA compliant homes for physically disabled vets. 

Click on the following link to view Major Mary being named among the top 125 women in the world:

http://www.thedailybeast.com/witw/galleries/2013/03/28/women-in-the-world-125-women-of-impact-photos.html

The award will be given to Major Mary Jennings Hegar at The Austin Toastmasters Club annual banquet, where Major Hegar will tell her story in a Keynote speech.  As one of the premier Toastmasters clubs in central Texas, The Austin Toastmasters Club also takes this time to honor and recognize their members with awards for Toastmaster of the Year, Best Speaker, Most Improved Speaker, Best Evaluator, and Best at Table Topics.  The Banquet, open to the public and other Toastmaster’s clubs, is held at “Green Pastures Restaurant,” an elegant banquet venue in Austin, Texas. 

Austin Toastmasters cordially invites you to join us in celebrating a time-honored tradition - Banquet Chair, Past President - Ian Muth

A workshop for small and medium-sized manufacturing and service businesses. 

The world has changed greatly during the last 100 years.  Yet many businesses still use costing methods that date back to the early twentieth century – when cost structures were very different to they are today.

How do you presently cost your products and services?  What basis do you use to decide how much ‘overheads’ to attribute to each of them?  What impact do those decisions have on your pricing policy, your sales and your profits?  Do you know?

If you haven’t recently taken time to re-evaluate whether or not the costing method you’re using is ‘right’ for your business, today, perhaps now is the time to do it?  It might be the most profitable couple of hours you’ll spend this year.

Product costing is critically important - but it doesn’t have to be complicated.  

This short workshop will look at some of the key issues and options we face when deciding what costing methods to adopt.

It will look at:

  • Identifying ‘Direct Costs’ from ‘Indirect Costs’ – and the changes that have occurred in these
  • Calculating the ‘Contribution’ generated by sales
  • Deciding how best to attribute ‘Overhead’ costs to different products
  • Recognising the different ‘Cost to Serve’ different customers
  • Identifying ‘profitable’ from ‘un-profitable’ products and customers
  • Using the information to ‘steer’ the business, more profitably.

Workshop Facilitator:

Leonard Brown is an experienced senior business manager who’s worked in both locally owned businesses and large corporates and in roles ranging through Finance, Operations Management and General Management.  Since 2007, he’s worked alongside client businesses as an Analyst, Trainer and Coach, helping them improve their profitability by them better understanding their costs and the different levels of contribution they earn from their different products, services and customers.

Leonard is a Chartered Management Accountant (FCMA) and holds an MSc in Business Improvement from the University of Ulster.
name: Time To Rethink Your Product Costing

The National Capital Regional Group of the Institute of Public Administration of Canada presents:

IPAC-NCR Annual General Meeting 2013:
Fostering Transparency in Public Administration

Featuring Susan Carter, Director, Transparency International Canada and Akaash Maharaj, Executive Director, Global Organization of Parliamentarians Against Corruption

When:  Wednesday, June 19, 2013

            5-5:30pm Registration and Cash bar 

            5:30-6:15pm Annual General Meeting and Elections

            6:15-7:30pm Panel Presentation on ‘Fostering Transparency in Public Administration’

Where: Army Officers’ Mess (149 Somerset West, Ottawa)

Price:   Complimentary for members, $20 for non-members 

RSVP:  Online by June 17 at About the presentation

The presence of transparency and the absence of corruption are key indicators of good governance.   Transparency International Canada is an NGO whose Mission is to be an informed voice that promotes anti-corruption practices and transparency in Canada’s governments, businesses and society at large.  The Global Organization of Parliamentarians Against Corruption (GOPAC) is an international network of parliamentarians that defines, tracks and initiates efforts against corruption in government at both the political and bureaucratic levels.   What is the impact of corruption in Canada and around the world?  What is the role of an independent public service in combatting corruption?  Has corruption become one of the defining public issues of our time?  Join us for this important discussion with Susan Carter, Director with Transparency International Canada, and Akaash Maharaj, Executive Director of GOPAC.

About the annual general meeting

IPAC NCR members will receive the Chairperson’s Report and the Treasurer’s Report, outlining the events and programs that IPAC has hosted in the past year.  Members will also elect the Regional Group Executive and Board of Directors for the upcoming year.  Please join us for our annual general meeting and meet the volunteers who deliver IPAC programming in the National Capital Region.

We are seeking nominations of IPAC members and other individuals to join our volunteer regional group executive. In particular, candidates are sought for the positions of Vice-Chair International and Vice-Chair Social Media and Web Communications. Please contact Howard Yeung at hoyeung@deloitte.ca for further information.

 

Le Groupe de la région de la Capitale nationale de l’Institut d’administration publique du Canada présente : 

Assemblée générale 2013 de l’IPAC – Groupe de la région de la Capitale nationale
Favoriser la transparence au sein de l’administration publique

L’assemblée mettra en vedette Susan Carter, directrice de Transparency International Canada, et Akaash Maharaj, directeur de l’Organisation mondiale des parlementaires contre la corruption.

Date et heure : mercredi 19 juin 2013

                         17 h à 17 h 30 : inscription et bar payant

                         17 h 30 à 18 h 15 : assemblée générale annuelle et élections

                         18 h 15 à 19 h 30 : présentation d’experts – Favoriser la transparence au sein de l’administration publique

Lieu : mess des officiers de l’armée de terre (149 Somerset Street West, Ottawa (Ontario))

Coût :  gratuit pour les membres, 20 $ pour les non-membres

RSVP : en ligne d’ici le 17 juin à

Au sujet de la présentation

La transparence et l’absence de corruption sont des indicateurs clés d’une bonne gouvernance. Transparency International Canada est un OBNL ayant pour objectif principal la lutte contre la corruption et la promotion d’une plus grande transparence au sein des gouvernements, des entreprises et de la société en général au Canada. L’Organisation mondiale des parlementaires contre la corruption (GOPAC) est un OBNL qui détermine et déploie des mesures pour lutter contre la corruption au sein des gouvernements, tant sur le plan politique qu’administratif. Quel est le niveau de corruption au Canada et ailleurs dans le monde, et quel est le rôle des fonctionnaires dans la lutte anticorruption? Venez assister à cette importante discussion à laquelle prendront part la directrice de Transparency International Canada, Susan Carter, et le directeur de GOPAC, Akaash Maharaj.

 

Au sujet de l’assemblée générale annuelle

Les membres IAPC de la région de la Capitale nationale recevront le rapport du président et le rapport du trésorier dans lesquels figureront tous les événements et tous les programmes que l’IAPC a organisés au cours de l’exercice précédent. Les membres éliront également les membres de l’équipe de direction et du conseil d’administration de la région pour l’exercice à venir. Joignez-vous à nous pour notre assemblée générale annuelle et venez rencontrer les bénévoles IAPC de la région de la Capitale nationale.

Nous sommes à la recherche de membres IAPC et d’autres personnes qui souhaitent se joindre à l’équipe de dirigeants bénévoles pour notre région, plus précisément pour les postes de vice-président, international; et de vice-président, médias sociaux et communications Web. Veuillez écrire à Howard Yeung à l’adresse hoyeung@deloitte.ca pour obtenir plus de renseignements.

  • User experience (UX)

  • Drawing the perfect mockups
  • Turning mockups into wireframes
  • Finding an app developer
  • APIs, data collection, and marketing

Note: This class is best geared towards utility apps rather than games.

description:
Inside Venture Capital

Iain Darroch, Ex-VC Investment Manager
Wednesday, June 26th from 6:30 - 8.00 pm

This 90 minute session takes you inside the world of venture capital, from the perspective of an Ex-VC. It will shed light on how a VC fund operates, how it manages investments and how these factors influence a VC’s decision-making pre and post investment.

Key topics and takeaways:

  • VC industry and fund structure
  • How a VC is incentivised
  • How VC assesses a deal
  • VC portfolio management
  • The VC–Entrepreneur relationship
  • Case studies and some fun anecdotes from the world of VC

This class is geared towards entrepreneurs, startup founders and employees, and anyone working in or interested in venture capital and corporate finance. The material covered will be equally applicable to companies who have already raised, and those that are looking to raise.

This class does not deal directly with how to raise venture capital. It is instead geared towards providing a foundational understanding of how venture capital works, what VC's look for, and shedding light on the industry. We'll be looking at case studies of situations that venture-backed startups might find themselves in (e.g. what happens when the money runs out?).

Iain Darroch has 5 years experience as a Venture Capitalist with Seraphim Capital in the UK and has worked on 45 investments. He has experienced the highs and lows of venture capital and wants to share it with you. More recently he worked with BSkyB in Emerging Products before moving to Sydney this year.

Diese Schulung richtet sich an alle neuen Kunden, die in der Excelumgebnung schnellstmöglich produktiv mit der Jedox Suite arbeiten möchten.  Schneller Planen. Präziser Analysieren. Einfacher Reporten. Wie verwandeln sie das meistgenutzte in das nützlichste Business Intelligence Tool?

  

Teilnahmevoraussetzungen

  • Es sind keine Vorkenntnisse über die Jedox Suite erforderlich
  • Es sind keine Vorkenntnisse im Bereich der mutlidimensionalen Datenhaltung erforderlich
  • Folgende Excelkenntnisse werden vorausgesetzt: 
    - Kenntnis über Datenhaltung in tabellarischer Form (Listen)
    - Kenntnis über die Möglichkeiten Formeln zu bearbeiten 
    (Formelassistent, Bearbeitungsleiste, F2-Modus, Aufbau von Formeln)
    - Kenntnis über den Umgang mit Verweisen (Fixierung mit F4)
    - Kenntnis der Formeln: summe(), wenn(), verketten(), sverweis() und des
    - Kenntnis des Namensmanagers

Schulungsziele

Nach der Schulung sind Sie in der Lage, in der Excel-Umgebung eine einfache Anwendung zu bauen, die ein grundlegendes Verständnis der folgenden Komponenten voraussetzt.

  • Model bauen (Dimensionen, Elemente, Attribute*, Würfel, 
    Elemente importieren* )
  • Berichte bauen (Ansicht einfügen, Elemente einfügen, Funktion einfügen, Subsets*)
  • Dateneingabe (Eingabe, Splashen, kopieren, Daten importieren*, Rules*)

*= Inhalte des  2.Tages

The Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC) invites you to participate in our 23rd Phillip Burton Immigration & Civil Rights Awards – The Time is Now, on Friday, May 31, 2013.
This is a momentous opportunity for the immigrant community and our nation. Comprehensive Immigration Reform is one of the most critical issues facing our nation today and the ILRC is at the forefront of advocating and advancing immigrant rights. The Phillip Burton Awards provide inspiring moments alongside some of our community’s most dedicated defenders of hard-working immigrants, including immigration attorneys, legal service providers, and community-based advocates.
The evening offers an opportunity to celebrate and recognize three very special guests committed to advancing immigrant rights. The Honorable Nancy Pelosi, Democratic Leader, will join us to present the inaugural Nancy Pelosi Award for Immigration and Civil Rights Policy to our Featured Speaker, the Honorable Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator. We will present the Immigration Advocacy Award to Jose Antonio Vargas, an outspoken journalist and courageous advocate.
This year’s honorees have demonstrated outstanding commitment, dedication, and leadership to advocating on behalf of the immigrant community throughout the nation. Please join with us as we celebrate their accomplishments and honor the legacy of immigrant rights pioneer, Phillip Burton.

description:
Trop Jr Roughcut would like to acknowledge the generous support of our Major Partner, The Australian Children's Television Foundation.

ABOUT

In 2012, Tropfest established Roughcut, a filmmaking symposium designed to cultivate outstanding storytelling on screen.

Now, in 2013, Trop Jr is excited to launch the inaugural Trop Jr Roughcut, designed to inspire and engage the next generation of successful Australian filmmakers.

The event will be a day-long series of conversations exploring creativity and collaboration. Featuring a diverse line up of speakers, all of whom have significantly contributed to the Australian film community, each session will focus on a different aspect of the filmmaking process.

Trop Jr Roughcut presents a fantastic opportunity for young filmmakers to learn from the industry’s best in an intimate and engaging environment.


TARGETING

Trop Jr Roughcut is targeted at students in years 5-10.

Designed to inspire kids aged fifteen and under, Roughcut will encourage kids to explore film making with confidence and creativity.


LINE UP:

Toby Morris

Toby is a full-time content creator for the film industry. Becoming involved in filmmaking at a young age, his talk will aim at inspiring others to follow a similar journey.

Jason van Genderen

An award-winning filmmaker, most recently taking out the Nokia Award at Sundance London, Jason will demonstrate creative ways to make films without fancy equipment and share his top ten do’s and don’ts for filming on a budget.

Eddie White

Eddie’s award-winning film The Cat Piano (narrated by Nick Cave) won awards at The Melbourne International Film Festival, Sydney Film Festival, Adelaide Film Festival and Australian Film Institute Awards as well as awards overseas. In this session he’ll talk about his career and how to get started with animation.

Guy Gross

One of Australia’s leading film and television composers and BAFTA-nominated composer of the score for Priscilla, Queen of the Desert, Guy will talk about that ever-important element of filmmaking, Music, and will discuss his career, his beginnings and how music can influence on-screen storytelling.

Actors Panel - David Jones Roberts, James Mackay and Wade Briggs
David, James and Wade, some of Australia's brightest names in acting, will speak in a general Q&A format. They will talk about how they started, how they collaborate with others, highs and lows, dreams and aspirations.

Kym Goldsworthy and Gina Roncoli

Kym and Gina, both multiple AWGIE (Australian Writers Guild Award) nominees and winners, have extensive experience in script writing and editing for both children and adult series. They will be talking about the screenwriting process and writing compelling pieces for both film and television.


TEACHERS TICKETS

For groups of ten or more students, one complimentary teacher ticket will be made available.

Please email Grace at gmcbride@tropfest.com.au for more information.


Additional tickets for teachers or guardians, or tickets for those bringing groups smaller than ten students, are available at the same price as a student ticket and can be purchased via this page.

description:
Walking the Marriage Minefield

Techniques for successful individual marriage counseling.

 

June 28, 2013

8:30am – 12:00pm (Registration begins at 8:00)

The Family Center of Gap - Upper Room

 

Individual marriage counseling happens every day. When one spouse is reluctant or refuses to go to counseling it may seem like all hope is lost, but it is possible to naviagate this challenging minefield and encourage couples to grow, one person at a time.

In this seminar Brad Aldrich, Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist and Director of Family Resource and Counseling Centers, will share methods and techniques he's employed to encourage positive changes even when only one spouse attends marriage counseling.

Core topics covered:

  • Principles of marriage counseling when only one person starts in counseling
  • Techniques to encourage changes even before couples counseling begins
  • Ways to improve the chance the absent spouse will come to counseling
  • How to show care without compounding the marriage problems
  • Discuss how to focus on individual’s issues without placing blame on the absent spouse
  • How Christian faith integrated with professional counseling techniques gives individuals a place to start signifigant changes. 
Participants will:
  • Understand the potential benefits and risks of an individual beginning marriage counseling even if their spouse is unwilling.
  • Learn techniques to encourage the absent spouse to participate in counseling.
  • Learn methods and techniques that will allow them to challenge individual clients to make changes in their marriage.
  • Learn what to watch out for when counseling any individual client who is married.

This seminar is approved for 3 continuing education units from the PA State Board of Social Workers, Marriage and Family Therapists and Professional Counselors.


Who should attend:
This seminar is designed to help any counselor, pastor, or mentor who comes in contact with individuals who are married.

description:
Thursday, June 13


The Next Stage of CSR for Canada: Hybrid Corporate Legal Structures and the Growth of Social Enterprise


Carol Liao

University of British Columbia, Faculty of Law

Respondent: Christie Stephenson, Manager of Environmental, Social and Governance Evaluations and Research at NEI Investments

 

$95 for all 3 webinars in the series - please contact the Event Organizer or schang@cbsr.ca if you have already previously paid.

This event is free for CBSR Members. Please enter your CBSR Member password as a promotional code for access. If you have forgotten your password, please contact the Event Organizer or schang@cbsr.ca

If you are affiliated with CBERN or the Ethics Centre, please contact Michael Windle, mwindle@cbern.ca for a complimentary pass code (limited availabilities).


The period when corporate social responsibility (CSR) only referred to corporate philanthropic donations has passed. Present day CSR is intimately intertwined with sustainable development, and its growth in the last several decades has been evident in Canada. The recent appearance of “hybrid” corporate legal structures on the international stage marks a growing trend toward enabling the dual pursuit of economic and social mandates for businesses. It suggests that the next significant stage in the CSR movement will be in the reformation and creation of corporate legal models that not only enable, but require, CSR concepts to be embodied within corporate governance practices.

While the US shareholder primacy model is often presumed to be the model that is dominant in modern Canadian corporations, this presumption is flawed. This article identifies some of the fundamental legal features that set Canada apart from US shareholder primacy, and attempts to demarcate a path for Canada to attain transformational corporate governance through its laws. The term “transformational” is borrowed from the business sector to help identify a tangible goal for corporate governance reform in Canada. Highlights include having a sustainable purpose, long term vision, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. Canada is poised to become a leader in corporate governance reform on two fronts: through the reformation of its existing laws regulating mainstream corporate governance practices, and in the creation of hybrid laws that can meet growing demands to legally house and govern social purpose businesses and enterprises.

There has been much fanfare surrounding the possible implementation of a hybrid similar to the US “benefit corporation” in Canada in order to address growing for-profit sector needs to pursue social value in addition to profit-making. However, some of the fundamental legal characteristics within the benefit corporation actually parallel existing common laws in Canada regarding mainstream corporate governance practices. Canada does not need to adopt American solutions to American problems. During these formative years of Canada’s corporate legal development, it is critical that the nation’s progressive legal stance is properly understood and taken into account when establishing hybrid laws so as not to confuse and/or jeopardize that stance. An ongoing stream of thoughtful and intelligent commentary is needed to address and advance Canadian corporate legal needs for social progress, as well as the establishment of innovative new hybrid laws that can bridge the gap between for-profit and non-profit sectors.


Click here to read the paper on Social Science Research Network (SSRN)

 

For more information, please visit: http://www.cbern.ca/researchdirections/liao/


Speaker Bio


Carol Liao is a PhD Student at the UBC Faculty of Law and incoming SJD Candidate at the University of Toronto Faculty of Law, where she is embarking on a unique joint collaborative program with the two universities. She specializes in corporate law and governance, corporate social responsibility, and law and economics.

Carol is a Liu Scholar at the Liu Institute for Global Issues. She holds a SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship, UBC Four Year Fellowship, and is the winner of the 2012 Robert Bertram Doctoral Research Award issued by the Canadian Foundation for Governance Research. She has published several articles in her field, including in the Ottawa Law Review and the Canadian Review of Social Policy.

Prior to entering graduate studies, Carol was a Mergers and Acquisitions attorney at Shearman & Sterling LLP (New York), where she represented public and private multinational corporations in a host of complex legal transactions and governance matters. She held a judicial clerkship at the BC Court of Appeal in 2003-2004, and is a recipient of the Wesbrook Scholar designation (UBC’s highest student honour).

 

Research Directions Webinars with CBSR

 

 

The Research Directions webinar series will feature research presentations from three PhD students working in different disciplines at universities across Canada. The webinar series will be scheduled for June 2013 and hosted by Canadian Business for Social Responsibility (CBSR).

Three papers will be selected for the Research Directions series in the weeks following the workshop, and decisions will incorporate feedback from all those who participated during the weekend workshop. Criteria include:

  • translates well to a cross-sector audience
  • well-timed and addressing a current need in the Canadian and/or global context
  • academic rigor and appropriate method for addressing the research question
  • demonstrated skill in presentation and responding to feedback

During each 50 minute webinar, the PhD student will present their research (10 minutes) and will receive feedback from faculty and non-faculty advisors, and a peer researcher at another university (15 minutes). The webinars will conclude with a facilitated discussion involving the webinar participants and the PhD student.

About Oaktoberfest:

Oaktoberfest celebrates the history, the flavors, and the people of the Bay Area. Oakland’s Dimond District hosts this one-of-a-kind Fall Festival, welcoming thousands with craft beer & food, entertainment, arts, and ecology. The Dimond continues a tradition as an entertainment destination, begun in the early 1900’s when Beer Gardens and German vacation resorts lined the boulevard. Oaktoberfest will bring world-class beer to the tented beer hall, serving steins of traditional German flavors and regional brew pub favorites.

Highlighting this years festival will be a traditional Biergarten, Eco Fair, Kid’s Area with Root Biergarten, German style homebrew competition featured in the homebrewers’ alley, and vendors from around the Bay. Celebrate Oktoberfest, Oakland style, in the Dimond at Fruitvale and MacArthur.

Hosted by the Dimond Improvement Association and the Dimond Business & Professional Association, the Oaktoberfest event brings together elements of the district vision for a one day, everyone welcome, family-friendly craft beer festival.

Oaktoberfest is an event designed not only to celebrate the proud history of a shining district in Oakland, but also to raise funds for improvement projects, community development programs, and future events. The success of this festival relies on committed volunteers and the generosity of area residents and engaged businesses. Your support for this non-profit event will create positive change in the community.

  • Music
  • Food
  • Beer
  • Eco Fair and Kid’s Area
  • Homebrew Competition and Homebrew Alley

The Music

Traditional sounds of Munich will be performed on the streets, stages, and in the Biergarten. The main Oaktoberfest Stage will also feature modern sounds from renowned area artists.

Gather around the Family Stage to see acts highlighting local performers, and children’s entertainment.

Instrumentalists and dancers will keep the steins swinging with entertainment around the beer hall and throughout the event.

Visit our Entertainment Page for this year’s line-up.

The Food

German delicacies from Bratwurst to Strudel will be found next to other regional cuisines and street fare. Sample dishes from a host of vendors or fill your plate with your favorite. It’s dining in the Beer Hall!

The Beer

20 breweries from around the Bay Area will be pouring German styles and Craft Beer classics. Oakland’s own Linden Street Brewery, Oakland Brewing Company, Pacific Coast Brewing and nearby Drakes Brewing Company will be alongside breweries from Santa Cruz to Sonoma and San Francisco to Sacramento. The Beer Hall will also host local wineries offering excellent regional varieties.

Eco Fair and Kid’s Area

The Eco Fair will ensure an engaging stroll through exhibits and information booths, drawing from a wealth of local non-profits, and corporate partners like Kaiser and Waste Management.

Interactive games, crafts, and displays will be featured in the Kid’s Area courtesy of Dimond Library, Oakland Parks and Rec, and Komodo Toys. Celebrate an active day with a stein of root beer and Dreyer’s ice cream from the Root Biergarten. Sit down and enjoy some children’s entertainment presented on the Family Stage.

Homebrew Competition & Homebrewers’ Alley

Homebrewers, fire up your kettle and excite some tasters, this years event will showcase a BJCP/AHA sanctioned all German style homebrew competition. Hosted by the Bay Area’s own Mad Zymurgists homebrew club.

description:
IBS Study Day – Yorkshire Branch

Description: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a common chronic condition; prevalence in the UK is estimated between 10 and 20% of the population.  Multi-factorial in nature, it is often challenging to treat; dietary manipulation alone may not be sufficient to resolve symptoms.  As dietitians, we need to have an awareness of all possible causes, including gut physiology and psychological issues, in addition to keeping abreast of emerging evidence, such as gluten-sensitivity, neurogastrology, pharmacological treatments and the new dietary intervention – FODMAPS. 

Our study day aims to address IBS in a holistic manner – and broaden our understanding of both the syndrome and the patient.  Due to the commonness of the condition, whether as a primary reason for referral, or as a factor underlying other health issues, our programme of specialist speakers is designed for all dietitians.

Provisional Event Programme

09.00 - 09.15    Registration, Tea/Coffee

09.15 - 09.30    Welcome

09.30 - 10.15    Medical Management of IBS - Dr Alex Ford

10.15 - 11.00    Dietetic Management of IBS and the IBS Network Self Care Plan - Julie Thompson RD

11.00 - 11.15    Comfort Break

11.15 - 12.00    The FODMAPs Approach - Helen Davies RD

12.00 - 12.45    Food and Mood; the Psychological Management of Food Intolerance - Prof. Nick Read

12.45 - 13.30    Lunch

Our speakers include:

Dr Alexander C. Ford MBChB, MD, FRCP (Senior Lecturer in Medicine and Honorary Consultant Gastroenterologist, Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust), presenting medical management, medications, diagnosis and patient pathways. Dr Ford’s areas of research interest are functional gastrointestinal disorders and inflammatory bowel diseases. He is an Associate Editor for Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics, and has published over 140 peer-reviewed articles and book chapters, including original scientific papers in JAMA, BMJ, Gastroenterology, Gut, Archives of Internal Medicine, and The American Journal of Gastroenterology.

Julie Thompson, Clinical Lead Dietitian, BSc (Hons) Dietetics, BSc Polymer Science & Technology. Qualified with a first class degree in Dietetics in 2007 and was awarded the Tunbridge prize. Part of the dietetic team at Calderdale & Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust, specialising in gastroenterology and bariatric dietetics. She also has a private clinic at the BMI hospital at Huddersfield. She is an executive on the board of The IBS Network, the UK charity for people with IBS (www.theibsnetwork.org) and has experience in treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with diet, including being trained to use The Low FODMAP dietary approach to reduce functional bowel symptoms. She has written for the Guardian, Sainsbury's Magazine, Network Health Dietitians Magazine, GUT Reaction and NACC local group magazine. Regularly writing posts for the blog (www.clinicalalimentary.wordpress.com) has promoted worldwide interest; the site contains recipes, book reviews and lifestyle advice in the area of gut health and diet. Professionally, she is a member of the Gastro Specialist Group of The British Dietetic Association and enrolled on the working group for developement of UK guidelines on IBS and diet and is also a member of Dietitians in Obesity Management.

Helen Davies, Senior Specialist Dietitian, BSc (Hons) Dietetics. Helen Davies has been with Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust since 2002 and she is a senior specialist dietitian within the gastrointestinal team with a particular interest in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Helen Davies received FODMAPs training at King's College London during 2012 and has been implementing the FODMAPs approach for selected IBS patients and is also trialing it in the treatment of IBD.


Prof. Nick Read MA, MD, FRCP (Chair of The IBS Network) is the chair and Medical Adviser of The IBS Network, the national charity for IBS and has recently coordinated The IBS Self Care Plan on its website www.theibsnetwork.org. He is presenting psychological and alternative treatments for IBS and introducing IBS Care Plan. Prof. Read works in private practice as a gastroenterologist and psychotherapist, helping people cope with illnesses, like IBS, that have no clear cause or pathology. During a long academic career, he has held university chairs in Gastrointestinal Physiology, Human Nutrition and Integrated Medicine, published many papers and several books including ‘Sick and Tired; healing the illnesses, doctors cannot cure’ (Phoenix, 2006). He now devotes much of his time trying to help people understand what underlies their illnesses and how better to manage them

With the selection of speakers, sponsorship support and opportunity to gain skills, knowledge and network, this is a morning not to be missed -  we look forward to seeing you!


How to find us

Venue:

Cookridge Conference Centre, Level 7, Bexley Wing, St James’ University Hospital, Beckett Street, Leeds, LS9 7TF

Phone: 0113 2433144

How to get there:

By car: Use postcode LS9 7TF as satnav reference. From Beckett Street turn into Alma Street and follow round to the multistory car park.

By Bus: Services 16, 42, 49 and 50 all run from Leeds city centre to St James’ University Hospital. Ask your bus driver for Beckett Street, Bexley Wing. Signs will direct you from the entrances to the venue. Neither bus service stops at the bus station, but staff can direct you to the nearest stop. www.wymetro.com offers a journey planner for bus services in Leeds.

By Train: Leeds is well connected to train services from all over the UK. From the train station take a bus to St James’ University Hospital as detailed above or take a taxi. Leeds City Taxis run from in front of the train station. Cheaper private taxis run from the back of the station by the Wetherspoons pub. Amber Cars (0113 2311366) and Apollo Cars (0113 2433333) are two such companies. Other taxi company numbers will be available from Leeds Tourist Information Office, situated on the station concourse. They can also supply city maps, give directions and advise on activities to help you enjoy the rest of your day.
