description:
Announcing... KRAKEN BINGO (drum roll folks)

Are you looking for a fix? Tired of grey skies and damp coats? Need a break from the humdrum of your lackluster wintery Melbourne life? Look no further! It's time to string up your lucky rabbit's paw and come join us for Kraken Bingo, a theme night filled with mischief, mayhem and B-I-N-G-O at Mr Wow's Emporium on Wednesday the 26th June 2013.

Kamp Kraken (an unlikely gag of misfits, eccentrics and travellers) are taking bingo back from lilac-haired old ladies and cranky old men to bring you a night out on the town that is definitely NOT for the faint of heart. It may be bingo, but it’s not for geriatrics. It's the first in a series... expect lewd jokes, great music, outrageous costumes and more fun than you have any right to expect from a set of spinning balls and random numbers.

Asda is the second largest supermarket retailer in the UK with over 500 stores located across the country, including around 60 in Scotland, ranging from large supercentres and superstores to the smaller format local supermarkets.  

The retailer has a dedicated Scottish sourcing team who have been working with local suppliers for many years to bring affordable quality products to their shoppers and now offers more than 900 local food and drink products. The team are continually looking to grow the local range and are interested in meeting food and drink companies with the potential to supply their Scottish stores.

The Opportunity

Asda are looking for locally produced products across all food and drink grocery categories within ambient, chilled and frozen.

Products must be retail ready and packaged suitable for merchandising in the supermarket fixture.  Companies must have capacity to manage volumes and consistent supply and be able to deliver direct to store or via the Regional Distribution Centres in Falkirk (Chilled) and Grangemouth (Ambient Grocery).  Suppliers must be SALSA accredited or be working towards this.


The Opportunity with Asda comprises the following:

Meet the Buyer

Companies are invited to apply for a one-to-one Meet the Buyer session with the Scottish team.  This is an excellent opportunity to meet the team, present your products and discuss how they fit with Asda’s trading requirements.

The one-to-one meeting will last up to 30 minutes. Briefing guidance will also be provided.    
 
This opportunity is open to any Scottish fresh, ambient or frozen food and beverage supplier interested in supplying Asda in Scotland.

description:
Welcome to the Charity People ‘Meet the CEO’ event with John Bird.

This is an opportunity for senior leaders within the charity and not for profit sector to build their knowledge, meet their peers in a relaxed and informal environment and listen to a presentation from a key industry CEO. If you’re interested in moving into the bosses chair then this will be an interesting session for you.

The evening will hosted by David Lale, Founder and Managing Director of Charity People and the guest speaker is John Bird, founder of The Big Issue.

John Bird grew up in an orphanage and served time in a young offenders institution, often sleeping rough with London’s homeless. Gradually he realised that the only way out of the destructive circle was to give himself a hand up rather than wait for others to give him a hand-out. Settling down in his 20’s he began to hold down regular jobs in factories and eventually as a skilled printer.

John never forgot the hardship of his youth and how similar deprivation afflicts tens of thousands of others. In 1992, John harnessed his knowledge of the print industry with a social vision which led to the founding of The Big Issue, sold by the homeless for the homeless with publisher and vendor splitting the proceeds. In transforming himself from being part of society’s problem into part of the solution, John has become a globally admired social entrepreneur.

The format for the evening is:

6pm – Registration and welcome drinks
6.30pm – Introduction from David Lale
6.40pm – Presentation by John Bird, Q&A and discussion
7.30pm – 9pm – Drinks and networking

Tickets cost £10, which includes a welcome drink (£5 from each ticket sold goes to The Big Issue Fundation)

Places are limited so please book as early as possible, we look forward to meeting you.

The small print
The venue may be an upstairs room that is not accessible for wheelchair users or those who have difficulty with stairs.
As with most events, things can change last minute, and we reserve the right to substitute speakers without warning. We also reserve the right to change location to another Central London location in keeping with demand for an event. Come see and get tactile with amazing homemade technology at Toronto Mini Maker Faire! For two days, tinkerers, artists and hackers from all over the GTA are leaving their garages to participate in Toronto’s greatest show and tell!

Join dozens of makers as they show off their projects and share what they know. Whether you’re a newbie or expert, you’ll get the chance to learn and make through interactive activities and workshops. Don’t miss out on the two-day Faire which is guaranteed to be fun, inspiring and surprising!

Come to Toronto Mini Maker Faire to...
    • Make your first robot
    • Get inspired to design your own wearable electronics
    • Learn how to solder
    • Take your skills up a notch by attending a hands-on workshop
    • Find a project that inspires you and talk to the maker who built it

If you're a creator or want to learn to create, Toronto Mini Maker Faire is the place for you!
name: Toronto Mini Maker Faire 2013
org_desc:
About Maker Faire:

Maker Faire is the Greatest Show (and Tell) on Earth—a family-friendly showcase of invention, creativity and resourcefulness, and a celebration of the Maker movement. It’s a place where people show what they are making, and share what they are learning.

Makers range from tech enthusiasts to crafters to homesteaders to scientists to garage tinkerers. They are of all ages and backgrounds. The aim of Maker Faire is to entertain, inform, connect and grow this community.

The original Maker Faire event was held in San Mateo, CA and in 2013 celebrated its eighth annual show with some 900 makers and 120,000 people in attendance. World Maker Faire New York, the other flagship event, has grown in three years to 500+ makers and 55,000 attendees. Detroit, Kansas City, Newcastle (UK),Rome, and Tokyo are the home of “featured” 2013 Maker Faires (200+ makers), andcommunity-driven, independently organized Mini Maker Faires are now beingproduced around the United States and the world—including right here in Toronto.

About MAKE Magazine:

MAKE is the first magazine devoted entirely to Do-It-Yourself (DIY) technology projects. MAKE unites, inspires, informs, and entertains a growing community of resourceful people who undertake amazing projects in their backyards, basements, and garages. MAKE celebrates your right to tweak, hack, and bend any technology to your will. Subscribe here.

Besides the magazine and the faire, MAKE is:

  • a vital online stream of news and projects, blog.makezine.com;
  • a retail outlet for kits and books, the Maker Shed;
  • a steady stream of fun and instruction via our YouTube channel;
  • Make: Projects, a library of projects with step-by-step instructions
  • a book publishing imprint with best-in-category titles on introductions to electronics, Raspberry Pi, Arduino and more.

프로그래밍 경험이 전혀 없는 분을 대상으로 기존의 디자인 프로그램이나 수작업으로는 구현이 불가능한 비쥬얼을 오픈소스 프로그램인 Processing을 이용해한 간단한 비주얼 프로그래밍을 배우고, 최종적으로 간단한 아트웍을 만들어 봄으로 Generative Art 입문을 위한 시간이 될 것입니다.  

 

 참가 대상 

  • 포토샵과 같은 기존의 툴에 한계를 느끼고 나만의 비주얼이나 필터 효과를 만들어 보고 싶은 디자이너. 
  • 기존의 작업 한계에서 벗어나 새로운 방식과 영감을 얻고 유니크한 작업물을 만들고 싶은 아티스트.
  • 새로운 접근방식을 통하여 유니크한 패턴을 작업하고 싶은 패션디자이너.
  • 그리고 프로그래밍 경험이 전무하지만 Generative Art 에 관심이 있는 모든 분.

 윤용호 [ Dofl Y.H. Yun ] 

Interactive Technologist at Firstborn

http://www.thedofl.com 


윤용호는 지난 12여년동안 인터렉티브 개발자로 활동해오고 있으며 한국, 홍콩, 영국 그리고 현재 미국에 이르기까지 인터렉티브 디자인을 주도하는 리더로서 인정을 받아오고 있다. 특히 최근에는 물질 공간과 인터렉션 디자인과의 교차점들을 찾는 작업들을 하고있다. 런던 예술대학에서 Interactive Media 석사를 전공하였으며 그의 졸업작품인 “Ensemble - Interactive Musical Instruments"는 Flashforward Film Festival 2008 San Francisco에서 ‘Experimental/Art’ 부문을 수상하였으며 2008 Adobe Design Achievement Awards에도 노미네이션되었다.


윤용호는 2007년에 세계정상의 디지털 샵인 런던에 위치한 Unit9에서 인터렉티브 개발자로 일하며 Philips, Samsung, Nestle, Heineken과 같은 클라이언트들을 위한 웹 사이트 개발을 하였으며 특히 유명한 "Got Milk?" 캠페인 작업을 하였다.이후 2009년 8월에 뉴욕으로 건너와 현재까지 디지털 에이전시인 Firstborn에서 SoBe와 Wrigley와 같은 클라이언트 작업들을 해오고 있다. Computer Vision,  Multi-touch와 같은 테크닉을 이용한 작업들에 중점을 두고 있으며 한 예로 ‘DoflBall’이라는 아이패드 게임은 단순히 사람과의 플레이가 아닌 애완동물들과의 플레이가 가능하도록 접근한 게임으로 큰 관심과 함께 성공을 거두었다... Read More >

Are you passionate about Technology and startups? Do you want to work for one?Not sure how to get your “foot in the door” for this dynamic, developing job market?


NY Career Meetup will answer these tough questions and much more!


Tech Startup Recruiter Roundtable for Job Seekers 


This exclusive, info-packed event will feature experienced Tech/Startup recruiters, a professional career coach, lots of experience and one agenda:

'How to get a job at a startup'



Who Should Attend?

 Those professionals looking for real world answers and savvy, inside info on the NYC startup tech community, including:


-‘Must-know’ facts before you apply: the NYC startup job market culture, trends

-What companies are hiring and “hot jobs”

-Strategic ways to search for startup jobs
-How to develop a successful relationship with a recruiter

-How to market yourself and stand out as a candidate
-What startup recruiters look for in a resume before they proceed for big ticket job And more!


NOTE: This exclusive, intimate event provides you with targeted networking and learning opportunities with very seasoned and successful recruiters and career professionals.  Meet them in person, form partnerships, and learn the formula of finding a job at a startup.

 

Early bird online registration- $15 (ends 06/23)

Regular online registration - $20 (ends 06/27)

 

Moderator:

Vicki Aubin, Career Coach

 


Vicki Aubin – The Rockin’ Career Coach is based in New York City and helps rising professionals kick-start the career of their dreams. With over a decade in Human Resources and Recruiting, she offers smart, savvy strategies for a kick-ass career they never taught you in (or out of!) college.  A featured guest on LinkedIn’s Ask the Expert Series and a volunteer career counselor at New York University, Vicki regularly guest blogs for several popular career websites and is the author of 22 Secrets to a Kick-Ass Interview:

http://bit.ly/Kick-AssInterview

 

Panelist:

Heather Reynolds, Talent Acquisition, Service Model Transformation, Avon

 

Heather is a Technical Recruiter/Social Media/Sourcing/Talent Acquisition Consultant with over 15 years’ experience working within high technology companies/projects within eCommerce, Mobility, SAP, in both large/small companies, established and start up's in NYC and throughout the USA.

http://www.linkedin.com/in/heatherreynolds

 

Panelist:

Brandi McMillian, Account Recruiting Manager at TEKsystems

 

Brandi has spent over half a decade providing staffing and consultative services to business clients with Digital IT initiatives over web, tablet, mobile, and social platforms. Her specialty is application recruiting, including but not limited to Flash/ActionScript, Front end developers (HTML/CSS, JavaScript), XML, PHP, LAMP, UI Developers/ Designers, IA's, User Experience Analysts, Business Analysts, Project Managers/ Coordinators, .NET developers, Java Developers, and SQL/ ORACLE/ SYBASE Developers/ DBA's.

http://www.linkedin.com/in/brandimcmillian

 

 

 

About NY Career Meetup


NY Career Meetup connects job seekers with Managers and Employers who make hiring decisions through its events.The group connects job seekers and Recruiters, Hiring managers and Employers and gives them a chance to know about employment opportunities and gather information about companies/ individuals who are currently hiring for both part time and full time positions.

The group gives job seekers best opportunity to make connections face to face with Managers and Employers.NY Career Meetup and its events allow the opportunity for both parties to check possibilities for prospective employment.

NY Career Meetup provides great opportunity for Job search networking Or Career Networking.60% of all jobs are found by networking. It's true, some of the best jobs are never advertised. Many are filled by successful job seekers who networked with the right people and got the job before it was ever advertised. Employers love referrals and first look to tap their own workers for people they know that can fill open positions. It's cheaper and provides for more quality employees. People do business primarily with people they know and like. Resumes and cover letters alone are often too impersonal to convince employers to hire. Networking makes you a recommended member of a much smaller pool. Networking leads to information and job leads, often before a formal job description is created or a job is announced. There is more to successful networking than just talking to your friends. To be a successful networker you must have as many contacts as possible hear your pitch and understand that you are in the job market.

Join NY Career Meetup

The group is for Job Seekers:
1) Connect with the Recruiters, Hiring managers and Employers who make the real hiring decision.
2) Learn about the companies who are hiring for full time positions and what kind of jobs are out there.
3) At group events meet Recruiters, Hiring managers and Employers face to face and discuss questions and concerns.Meet photographers who are looking for models, website builder who needs web-disgners etc
4) Make a great first impression on the manager and get in the circle of recommended candidates which is a much smaller pool from the candidates who are serious.

The group is for Managers and Employers;

1) Through NY Career Meetup network meet High-quality professionals at each event. The group helps in connecting companies with professionals who may not have otherwise known about the opportunities that it has to offer.
2) Meet professionals in Person; Going over resumes, scheduling interviews and the actual interview process is very time-consuming. Group events will gives Managers and Employers the opportunity to meet a large number of professionals in person and even conduct one on one session. This makes it easy to quickly weed out individuals whose background and personalities might be a good fit.

3)Publicity for Company The group and its events enable Recruiters, Hiring managers and Employers to publicize their company to other group members and promote it at group's events.

4) Saves Money; The group events helps you meet the right professional the first time thereby reducing the HR, marketing and other overhead costs.

Job Search Networking / Career Networking Tips

1) Make an impression quickly when you first meet someone and try and get your story across before the conversation ends.
2) Create an inventory of your accomplishments, including your educational background and work history, to keep at hand should a chance encounter become a contact.
3) Make a list of the assets you will bring as a prospective employer at the group events
4) Bring resume, business card and a pen.Write some notes so you'll remember the details on who you have just met on the business cards you collect or in a notebook
5) Try to get a business card, phone number, setup a future lunch, etc., Basically, some method of future contact or follow-up so that you can develop this further.

This is a forum for job seekers to expand their networks, learn secrets from top HR managers and recruiters, and secure new opportunities.

Come and Introduce yourself to others in the industry while enjoying some casual conversations, a drink, and a brief informative discussion of the the topic of the night.

Find out what your are really worth on the street,Wall Street Or Main Street, stop being underpaid.

Our world is changing and the way we look for jobs and market ourselves must change as well.In today's tough job market, job seekers must maximize the use of their available resources. You have the skills, talent and passion - through this meet up you and others will be able to harness the power of an effective career networking toward a common goal - new and better opportunities!

org_desc:
The Jazzschool is an innovative nonprofit organization dedicated to the study and performance of jazz — America’s indigenous art form —and related styles of music from around the world. Founded in 1997, the Jazzschool is located in the historic Kress Building at Shattuck and Addison, in the heart of the Downtown Berkeley Arts District. The Jazzschool is part of a vibrant East Bay arts community that includes the Freight & Salvage, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, Aurora Theatre, East Bay Media Center and renowned Cal Performances at the University of California.

Hailed as one of the nation’s most comprehensive centers for jazz studies, the Jazzschool offers instrumentalists and vocalists of all ages and skill levels a broad spectrum of performance ensembles, lectures, workshops and private instruction. Courses are designed for the professional musician, the serious student and the jazz aficionado seeking personal enrichment. A multi-faceted institution, the Jazzschool comprises several key components.

Jazzschool Institute

The Jazzschool Institute is a music conservatory offering the aspiring professional a comprehensive 4-year degree program culminating in the Bachelor of Music in Jazz Studies. The Institute provides a challenging curriculum of performance, jazz theory and improvisation, ear training, composition, arranging, transcription and analysis, and music history courses, taught by professional artists and educators. Coursework also includes music business, music technology and financial planning, thoroughly preparing students for a fulfilling career in the performing arts.

Jazzschool Community Music School (JCMS)

The JCMS provides music education and performance opportunities for people of all ages and levels of ability. Consisting of the JCMS Adult Music Program and the JCMS Young Musicians Program, the JCMS operates year-round on a quarterly basis and offers over 100 ensembles, courses and workshops to build all aspects of musicianship. Students are routinely featured in concert performances, open to the public. With a formidable faculty of renowned musicians and educators, the JCMS is a cornerstone of the Bay Area’s thriving music scene.

JCMS ADULT MUSIC PROGRAM

The Jazzschool Adult Music Program offers life-enriching opportunities to learn about and play jazz and related styles of music from throughout the world. Courses are available for both instrumentalists and vocalists, and everyone from young adult to senior citizen is welcome. Instruction and performances occur primarily in late afternoons, evenings and on weekends, making the program easily accessible to the working professional.

JCMS YOUNG MUSICIANS PROGRAM

The Jazzschool Young Musicians Program offers middle and high school students of all skill levels a wide variety of combos, big bands and vocal performance courses throughout the entire year, as well as camps during the summer. Select ensembles participate in national competitions, and Jazzschool bands have routinely taken top awards from DownBeat, the Monterey Next Generation Jazz Festival and others.

Workshops

Visiting artists and Jazzschool faculty lead fascinating and practical workshops, typically a single session of two or three hours in length and held on a Sunday. Content may focus on any specific aspect of jazz theory or performance, such as playing in odd time signatures or the art of vocal improvisation. Past workshops have been taught by prominent musicians from Bobby McFerrin to Dave Liebman, Janis Siegel, Peter Erskine, Sheila Jordan, Nguyên Lê and others.

Concerts

The Jazzschool facility includes an intimate venue with seating capacity of 100. Throughout the year, Jazzschool faculty and students perform for the public, providing a real-world incubator for developing new concepts and gaining audience exposure in the competitive Bay Area environment. High-profile artists have performed at the Jazzschool, including Terence Blanchard, Art Lande, Kim Nalley, Taylor Eigsti, Sachal Vasandani and many more.

Jazzschool Books & Records

The Jazzschool’s in-house retail store is a treasure trove of jazz-related reading and listening materials. It provides students, teachers and the public with convenient access to extraordinary books, recordings, videos and accessories.

Jazzcaffè

Located within the Jazzschool facility, the Jazzcaffè serves up delectable fare for students and visitors to enjoy a convenient bite to eat. A changing menu features house-made soups, salads and sandwiches, as well as beer, wine, espresso and desserts. Drop by for a great meal to match the great music!

Transportation

The Jazzschool is easily accessible by car and public transportation. The downtown Berkeley BART station and AC Transit bus stops are within a block. There is a public parking garage just a few steps away on Addison, in addition to metered street parking throughout the neighborhood.

 

REFUND POLICY
Registration fees and first class tuition for classes are non-refundable. Requests to drop must be received in writing within 48 hours of the first class meeting in order to qualify for a refund; please visit the main office or e-mail drop@jazzschool.org to request a refund. Refunds for remaining tuition are not possible after the 48-hour drop deadline.

$100 per week of camp tuition is non-refundable; the remainder is refundable only until the cancellation deadline (see program information). Refunds are not possible after the cancellation deadline.

Tuition for intensives, workshops and short-term classes is non-refundable.

Exceptions may be granted only in the case of extremely serious medical or family emergencies; please enclose a doctor’s note and/or other supplementary documentation with your request. Please note that refunds will not be granted for classes dropped due to scheduling conflicts arising after the start of the session.

Please note: Refunds make take up to 30 days to process.

TICKETS SALES
All ticket sales are final. Refunds or exchanges are not possible.

Concert and workshop tickets are available online at By phone (Toll Free):1-866-384-3060 Monday–Friday 9am – 5pm
In Person at the Jazzschool, 2087 Addison Street, Berkeley. Monday – Saturday 10am – 5:30pm, Sundays 11am – 3pm
For more information please call the Jazzschool at (510) 845-5373

All concerts are $5 for students enrolled in the Jazzschool Young Musicians Program. Purchase a package of 5 or more concerts and receive a 20% discount!

All concerts are $5 for youth under 12. Discounted tickets available to seniors (65+) and students with valid ID.
Ticketing Policies: All ticket sales are final. Refunds or exchanges are not possible.

SEATING POLICY
Performances start promptly at the published time. Doors open 30 minutes  prior to performances. Seating is “open” and available on a first-come, first-served basis.
Please note: an advance sale ticket does NOT guarantee late comers a seat. Late comers may be asked to wait in the lobby until intermission or an appropriate interval to be seated.

EMAIL POLICY
Information collected by the mailing list form is used solely for the purpose of notifying you of Jazzschool events or related information that might interest you. We have no intent to sell or otherwise distribute your e-mail address and/or information to any other entity.

Making Sense of the Australian Curriculum - Yrs 6-9

Maths and Science 


A Far North, Eyre and Western, and Yorke and Mid North regions initiative focussed on the Middle Years (6-9) of schooling for DECD, Catholic and Independent school teachers and leaders

- in Port Augusta


Preparing for the Middle Years of Schooling in 2013 and beyond
Connecting teachers with the professional teaching associations


  • A conference by CEASA, in collaboration with the Primary Maths Association (PMA), the Mathematical Association of South Australia (MASA) and the SA Science Teachers Association (SASTA)
  • The day will be conducted by members of the professional teacher associations who have had significant  involvement with the Australian Curriculum.
  • These workshops will give participants practical knowledge, understandings and skills relevant to teaching of the Australian Curriculum Learning Areas of Maths and Science. There will support and time for planning lessons/units of work.

Program:
 
8.30 - 9.00am Registrations
9.00 - 9.15am Welcome
9.15-12.00pm Workshop Sessions A   -  Choice of 3 – Maths (x2), Science (x1)
12.00-12.45pm LUNCH
12.45-3.30pm Workshop Sessions B   -  Choice of 3 – Maths (x2), Science (x1)
3.30-3.45pm Feedback and Closing Session
 
 

PLEASE NOTE: NO REFUNDS WILL BE GIVEN LESS THAN 7 DAYS PRIOR TO THE EVENT

 

Workshops:
 
Workshops A - 9.15am - 12.00pm


A1: Exploring Mathematics Through the TfEl Lens

Lisa-Jane O'Connor

The Australian Curriculum provides the “what” and TfEL provides the “how”. So, what does this really look like in action in Mathematics? In 2012 DECD released the results of their TfEL research with teachers which highlighted significant gaps in teacher capacity to work with three of the TfEL aspects:

-                 2.3: Negotiate learning

-                 3.3: Explore the construction of knowledge

-                 4.3: Apply and assess learning in authentic contexts

This session will explore these particular areas and consider the range of strategies that might be used if TfEL was brought to the fore within a Mathematics learning programme.


A2:Learning Design in Maths

Carol Moule

Some of the questions and concerns that we frequently hear are

  • What should the Proficiencies look like in my classroom?
  • How can I differentiate my tasks to accommodate for the diverse needs and abilities of my students?
  • There is not sufficient time to cover all the content in the Australian Curriculum.... how do I do that?

While these questions and concerns are not new, the implementation of the Australian Curriculum presents an opportunity to review the pedagogy and learning design in mathematics teaching.

These workshops will model various rich tasks which:

  • Are activity-based
  • Are designed for enquiry based learning
  • Have multiple entry and exit points for students
  • Enable conceptual understanding
  • Address learning in more than one strand and/or curriculum area
  • Involve working  mathematically, as well as addressing all four proficiencies (Fluency, Understanding, Problem Solving and Reasoning)

The content will include collecting and analysing data, introductory algebra and geometry, and the use of technology.  Detailed notes will be provided.


A3: Planning with the Australian Curriculum: Science

Kate Dilger

What is the Australian Curriculum: Science? What do I teach? What activities can I do? Where can I find relevant and engaging activities and resources? This program will allow you to answer these questions and more.

You will work actively to plan with the Australian Curriculum documents using an inquiry based learning model in a workshop setting.  You will engage in a simple planning process using the 5 E’s and the Australian Curriculum documents. Develop your understanding of how you can effectively plan and teach an engaging science program. Immerse yourself in a hands-on, inquiry based science program based on the 5 E’s and use comprehensive planning templates to structure an exciting plan for science.

This workshop will provide teachers with explicit curriculum materials and contemporary pedagogical strategies to enable them to successfully plan using the Australian Curriculum: Science.  Each session is accompanied by handouts and activities that highlight practical ways of how actual lessons work. 

 
 
 
 
Workshops B - 12.45pm - 3.30pm


B1:Assessment Design in Mathematics

Lisa-Jane O’Connor

In 2012, all DECD sites had their first go at reporting using the Australian Curriculum in Mathematics. These new Guidelines required DECD teachers to use an assessment collection that had gathered information about the quality of the knowledge, skills and understanding children had demonstrated AS WELL as their capacity to apply and use these in a range of familiar and new contexts.

This session is designed to:

-                 Clarify what “quality of learning” for knowledge, skill and understanding means at your year level and the implication for your assessment collections in Mathematics

-                 Explore the meaning of “new contexts” and what this can look like in action including doing some assessment design for your particular year level

-                 Explore the range of assessment strategies that we can use to build a rich assessment collection/portfolio that positions us to be able to report effectively

-                 Explore the link between “new contexts” and the TfEL criteria 4.3, “Apply and assess learning in authentic contexts”


B2:Learning Design in Maths

Carol Moule

  • Enable conceptual understanding
  • Address learning in more than one strand and/or curriculum area
  • Involve working  mathematically, as well as addressing all four proficiencies (Fluency, Understanding, Problem Solving and Reasoning)

The content will include collecting and analysing data, introductory algebra and geometry, and the use of technology.  Detailed notes will be provided.


B3: Planning with the Australian Curriculum: Science

Kate Dilger

What is the Australian Curriculum: Science? What do I teach? What activities can I do? Where can I find relevant and engaging activities and resources? This program will allow you to answer these questions and more.

Sainsbury’s is the 3rd largest supermarket retailer with 16.8% share of the UK grocery market and recording year on year growth of 5.6%, making it the fastest growing amongst the leading four grocery retailers (IGD Retail Analysis 12 weeks to 12 May 2013). With over 1100 stores UK-wide, including 56 located in Scotland and plans to expand their Scottish network further, this is an opportunity not to be missed.  

Sainsbury’s have a dedicated team based in East Kilbride, whose priority is to grow the Scottish range and work with local suppliers to bring relevant and appealing Scottish products to their shoppers.  They are currently seeking branded and Sainsbury’s own label products and are interested in meeting food and drink companies with the potential to supply their Scottish stores.

The Opportunity

Sainsbury’s are looking for Scottish products across all food and drink grocery categories, as well as producers who may have the potential to supply Sainsbury’s Taste the Difference and By Sainsbury’s ranges. 

Products must be retail ready and packaged suitable for merchandising in the supermarket fixture.  Producers must have capacity to manage volumes and consistent supply and be able to deliver direct to store or via the Regional Distribution Depot in East Kilbride. Suppliers must have SALSA accreditation (as a minimum to supply their brand) and BRC accreditation (to supply Sainsbury’s own brand).

Meet the Buyer

Companies are invited to apply for a one-to-one Meet the Buyer session with the Scottish Buying team.  This is an excellent opportunity to meet the team, present your products and discuss how they fit with Sainsbury’s trading requirements.

The one-to-one meeting will last up to 30 minutes.  You will be allocated a time which will be advised in advance.  Briefing guidance will also be provided.

description:
SQL Server MVPs and blogging team Audrey Hammonds and Julie Smith of DataChix.com offer a training day chock full of data warehouse, ETL, and business intelligence goodness. Audrey will take you on a guided tour of converting a transactional model into Dimension and Fact tables. After the model has been created, Julie will guide you through loading those tables using SQL Server Integration Services. Finally, they'll show you how to present your data to users and give them the tools they need to make their business... intelligent.

 

Part I Dimensional Modeling with Audrey

 

Topics include:

So you have a transactional database... what's next?

Why Third Normal Form is Tough for Reporting

Aligning Business Needs with Your Modeling Plans

Getting started with Dimensional Modeling

From Codd to Kimball: How to get your data BI-ready

Facts about Dimensions and Facts

Here Comes the Grain Again: Granularity and You!

 

Part II Extract Transform and Load using SSIS with Julie

Topics include:

A tour of SSIS

Control Flow Basics

Data Flow Basics

How to load Dimensions with SSIS

How to load Facts with SSIS

Frameworks

What happened and when

Queing auditing and error handling

When things go wrong, how to know the details

Top quirks of SSIS—what, why, and how to get around them.

 

Part III Expand your BI Toolkit with Julie and Audrey

 

Topics include:

          DQS – Data Quality Services and ETL

          MDS – Master Data Services and the Data Warehouse

          PowerPivot – Convert business users into reporting experts

 

 About the Speakers

 

SQL Server MVP Audrey Hammonds is working as a Consultant for Innovative Architects in Atlanta. (With my fellow Datachix!) Fourteen years ago, she volunteered for DBA training to escape COBOL, and never looked back. A firm believer that good fundamentals and solid design can save a database professional’s sanity, she has devoted much of her career to designing (hopefully) elegant databases and straightening up others’ not-so-elegant databases. Audrey has run the gamut from Database Developer to Production DBA to Architect. 

 

 Julie Smith has spent the last 13 years bending data using varied tools such as MS Access, MySQL, and SQL Server 2000-2012. She is a Consultant at Innovative Architects, and an active speaker, blogger and writer in the Microsoft SQL Server Community. In spite of being a SQL Server MVP, she remains “very simple woman with warm fuzzy secret heart.”

description:
Overview

From climate change and superbugs to asteroid strikes, many of the most important, exciting and compelling stories of our era come from the world of science. But writing about science, health or the environment is a difficult task. The fields cover a vast array of different disciplines, new discoveries can be prone to over-hyping, and your success depends on explaining complex information to a lay audience, meaning digging out and making the most of good stories is hard work.

This evening course is the perfect primer for anyone interested in a career in science journalism or communication, as James Randerson, Guardian Environment and Science News Editor, shows how science stories make it from the lab bench to the media.

Through a series of talks and practical exercises, Randerson will teach you how to spot and write a potent, informative news story, and how to pitch it to editors. You'll learn about the major common sources journalists use to find stories about science, health and the environment. You'll also learn about the ways science journalism can go wrong, and how inaccurate stories make it into print.  Perhaps most importantly, you'll also learn how to avoid falling into the churnalism trap of reporting bad science and ensure your writing is both accurate and authoritative.

Sections on the best ways to employ digital media, and how the internet is changing the reporting of science means this is ideal for journalists and bloggers alike.

Tutor profile

James Randerson is the Guardian's environment and science news editor. He has previously worked as the paper's science correspondent and as deputy news editor for New Scientist magazine. He also has a PhD in Evolutionary Genetics.

He has lectured on science, health and environment journalism to students at universities including City, Cardiff and Bath. He also has experience of training academics in how the media works. He directed sessions at the 6th World Conference of Science Journalists in 2009 in London and at the UK Conference of Science Journalists last year.

Details

Date: Monday 12 August 2013

Times: 6.30pm-9.30pm

Venue: University of Salford, MediaCityUK, Plot B4, Salford Quays M50 2HE

Price: £39 (includes VAT, booking fees and refreshments)

Event capacity: 120

description:
Do you sometimes feel like a chicken with your head cut off?

Discover the difference between busy-ness and effectiveness. If you want less overwhelm, missed deadlines and mediocre results, bring your team to this practical, hands on workshop to learn how to be much more effective.

Just because you and your team are busy does not mean you are effective. Even the chicken whose head had been cut off can still run around. Effectiveness means getting exactly the output you need while spending the least possible energy.  Everything outside of this is waste.  When we don't make requests we are wasteful.  When we make unclear requests we are wasteful.  When we do not trust others to fulfill their promises, we are wasteful.  It is easily documented that managers and teams waste more than 25% of their time and energy.  Why?  Only because we haven't learned the tools to be more efficient.  Building trust, clear requests, grounded promises, committed action…..learning these as tools and building them as habits creates a team that is effective and connected.  

Busy-ness is no guarantee of effective action.  Effective action requires precise communication and trust.  If you feel overwhelmed, constantly behind or are unhappy with your results maybe you are busy but not effective.  It is a choice.  Come find out the difference.


Our presenter, Dan Newby is a Master Certified Coach; Mentor Coach and Lead Facilitator for Newfield Network's Coach Training Program.  Find out more about Newfield's Coach Training Program.

We will be providing light snacks and coffee, tea and water.   Please feel free to bring your own lunch or just enjoy the snacks, or both!

Doors will open at 1030am and we will begin promptly at 1100am.

We invite you to share this invitation with others that you feel would be interested in joining us and look forward to seeing you there.

 

Ila Edgar


PS:   This event is eligible for ICF continuing education credits and is also eligible for 2 continuing education credits for Certified Human Resource Professionals.  

Please contact me for more information.

TYCHO

Tycho is the music project of San Francisco artist and producer Scott Hansen. As Tycho, Hansen blends swirling melodies into vaguely triumphant arcs that crisscross between stuttering beats and vocal samples, creating rolling sonic landscapes that extend into the horizon. Known in the design world as ISO50, Hansen is famed for his bucolic, sun-drenched design style, which serves as a backdrop and mirror for his musical output. .

 

Many of Tycho’s productions play out like complete electronic dream pop songs in isolation rather than vignettes or extended mood pieces. Tycho debuted in 2002 with The Science of Patterns, a self-released four-track EP. Sunrise Projector, his first album, was released in 2004 on the Gammaphone label. After the 2006 album Past Is Prologue, recorded for Merck, he settled in with Ghostly International, where he released a trio of singles and EPs (“The Daydream,” “Adrift,” “Coastal Brake”) prior to the 2011 album Dive. ~ Andy Kellman, Rovi

.

 

In 2008, Tycho received a nod as one of URBmagazine’s “Next 100” artists to watch. Since 2007, Tycho, with great care, released sun-drenched, melodic singles for the 3 years, honing his sound and collaborating with even more live instrumentation. In 2011, his meticulous process sees the release of DIVE. The wait has been well worth it.

 

 


starkey-music.com
Starkey on Facebook
Starkey on Soundcloud		  

STARKEY

Starkey is blessed with musical arrangement skill’s that would leave most composers green faced with envy. This combined with his high production ethic makes him a formidable force not only in the underground but also as a super producer of the future. Starkey is yet another example of what the streets of Philadelphia can create, his sound hits hard and is littered with bass and colourful audio frequencies. If you like grime, dubstep, hip hop and all things “street bass” then Starkey’s hard edged spaced-out crunk is the sound for you. Starkey has been on fire in 2010 with his recent 2nd full length on Planet Mu and worldwide touring schedule, not to mention remixes for Kano, The Orient, Uffie and more.

 

His original grime and bass leaning productions can be heard throughout (his own Seclusiasis label is at forefront of Street Bass in the USA), especially on "'Rayguns" and "Blood Roses", but it's his compositional talents and more delicate blemishes seeping into his beats which are really starting to make Starkey stand out. Lead track "Open The Pod Bay Doors" is an epic statement of intent that builds in the most beguiling of ways, at once melodic, futuristic and tough

 

Starkey comes with much support. He has been heralded in Pitchfork, FACT, The Wire, DJ Mag, Radio 1 and chosen by Mistajam on 1Xtra as one of the first DJ's for his new Daily Dose of Dubstep residency. He has worked with Tinie Tempah, Trim, Virus Syndicate, Kozzie whilst co-writing/producing with the likes of Guy Sigsworth and Aaron Levinson. This EP will see Starkey build on the huge success of his Space Traitor EPs by pushing experimentalism in bass culture while maintaining a rich melodic and harmonic language. Don't be surprised to see Starkey producing for some of music's biggest names in the not too distant future.

  

 


andreilien.com
Andreilien on Facebook
Andreilien on Soundcloud		  

ANDREILIEN

Andrei Olenev first emerged as HEYOKA on the San Francisco underground glitch/bass scene in 2006. By 2009 he was touring extensively and quickly became a staple sound in the rapidly growing bass music scene of North America. With a constantly evolving, original style, he stood out amongst bass music producers as one who keeps the vibe going strong while venturing to explore new realms of sonic experience. Playing always live sets of his own original tracks, his music has been described as a journey through fractal soundscapes and alternate realms while riding the waves of fat glitch beats and earth rumbling sub bass.

 

Andrei has brought his signature sound to North American festivals including: Symbiosis, Sonic Bloom, Raindance, Lightning in a bottle, Big Bounce, Alchemeyez, and large Burning Man sound camps such as Nexus, El circo, Temple of Boom, Entheon Village, Roots Society and Fractal Nation. He has also played several international electronic music festivals such as Shambhala (Canada), Boom (Portugal), Earthfreq and Winter solstice (Australia), and Luminate (New Zealand). He frequently tours nightclubs and concert venues through the States and Canada, as well as internationally in Australia, New Zealand and Russia.

 

As Heyoka, Andrei released his first ep in 2008, and by 2011 had produced over six albums through San Francisco’s Muti Music, a leader in the glitch hop and bass music scene. In “Dub Iteration,” Andrei’s newest album and first official release as Andreilien, he revisits the dubby vibe of some of the earlier Heyoka releases with a newer fatter twist.

 

Further expanding artistic horizons, Andrei has been continually working to develop a multimedia project with original Visionary and 3D art to create full sensory fractal journey in a dimension of its own.

LEVYdance’s mission is to create art that ignites awareness of our shared human experience. The company is based in San Francisco's SOMA district at Dance Magazine). Levy's signature aesthetic is a vibrant landscape of physical action and reaction - under his direction, dance artists express personal narrative in physical currents, engaging and responding in cinematic scenarios of human intimacy.

Beyond performing in traditional venues, LEVYdance also creates installation performance experiences that seek to redefine the relationship between performer and audience. The company has blended new media and dance into an installation that invited the audience inside the performance space, performed as a flash mob at public outdoor sites, and seated audience members and dancers together at banquet tables for an interactive performance experience. LEVYdance's performance of ROMP was named one of the Bay Area's "Top Ten Dance Moments of 2011" by the San Francisco Chronicle and in 2013 LEVYdance received an Isadora Duncan Dance Award for Outstanding Achievement in Performance for their 2012 production of Low Down.

description:
Rhythmik Soul Productions is proud to present an amazing event aboard the Pioneer Princess sailing on the magical summery waters of Lake Ontario.


Join us at a magical evening featuring Award Winning Sitar Maestro Anwar Khurshid and the versatile Jazz sensation Paul Deslauriers. Both artists, renowned and masters in their genre will bring together a fusion of musical notes in the scintillating boat cruise in Lake Ontario. Sure to leave an everlasting impression on you, join us for this memorable evening as friends and help bring together the magic of music.


Anwar Khurshid, an award winning sitar player and recently accredited with his Sitar performance in four time Oscar Winning  hollywood blockbuster “Life of Pi”, grew up immersed in music. Before he made the sitar his primary focus, he studied Hindustani vocal, flute and tabla. These early instruments still permeate his playing, giving it a fluid, lilting quality that has become his signature. His major influences in the Hindustani tradition are Ustad Nasiruddin, Ustad Vilayat Khan Sahib and Ustad Amir Khan Sahib. He has performed in major cities in Europe, North America and Asia, including Toronto, Vancouver, New York, Ankara, Delhi, Lahore. He has composed music for dance and theatre, such as Umrao and Ballet Creole.  Being in Canada has allowed Anwar to play with musicians from other genres, including Blues music with Paul Deslauriers, Jazz with Bruce Cassidy, African music with Waleed Abdelhameed, Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese music . Through these innovative collaborations, Anwar creates music that transcends categorization.

Paul Deslaurier A virtuoso on both electric and acoustic guitars, Paul Deslauriers (pronounced “day-loree-ay”) is part of Canada’s guitar elite and is considered one of Quebec’s overall best guitarists; but it doesn’t stop there, he’s also a powerful and expressive singer. Winner of the Lys Blues Award for Best Artistic Performance in 2011, Album of the Year in 2008 (En Duo), and Best Musical Performance in 2005, he was also a nominated at the Canadian Maple Blues Awards in 2008 for Acoustic Act of the Year along with Dawn Tyler Watson for their album “En Duo”. In 2010 Deslauriers was musical director, producer, and performer on the “Nos Stars Chantent Le Blues à Montréal” CD for L’équipe Spectra and the Montreal International Jazz Festival. Paul’s 2006 solo release Ripping Into Red garnered rave reviews in the April 2007 issue of Guitar Player Magazine.
name: Cruise on Lake Ontario with Sitar-Blues Performances & Dinner

description:
FAQs

 

Do I have to bring my tools to the class?

No. This is a look-n-learn / Demo only so no need to bring your tools.

 

Do I have to use Keune in order to purchase a ticket?

Of course NOT! Keune is dedicated to ALL salon professionals, not just those that use Keune.

 

You won't try to sell me Keune will you?

No. There will not be product to purchase nor anyone trying to sell you anything. This is about creative techniques and formulations to create believable blondes. If afterwards you want to know more about Keune color and products those questions will be answered.

 

Will there be hand-outs at the class?

Yes! We provide you with head-sheets so you can map the techniques. It's also a good idea to bring your smart phone or camera to take pictures of the flip chart pages as well as the artist facilitating the class.

 

Will I receive CEU hours for this class?

This is NOT a CEU hour class for either GA or SC. However, you will receive a certificate for completion of the class.

 

Can I update my registration information?

Yes - after you register if you need to you may update your registration.

 

Do I have to bring my printed ticket to the event?

Yes please. We will also have a sign in sheet outside the classroom to check-in upon your arrival.

 

What is the refund policy?

You may receive a refund up to seven (7) days prior to the class. After that we can not issue refunds.

In the first of three IWDev Workshops in 2013 - Matt Ball will be giving an Introduction to Test-Driven-Development. This workshop is ideal for developers and students who are not already using TDD as part of their every day work, who would like to add another string to their bow. If you've heard the buzz and don't really know how or why to get started - this 1 day session will give you the answers.

In this one-day hands on workshop, we will cover:

  • Test-Driven-Development as a methodology - what is it, and why is it important?
  • Why to write tests-first, rather than afterwards.
  • Outside-In and End-to-End testing and development.

  • Hands-on sessions that will get you up and running developing code from requirements, through to tests and then production code - as well as bug hunting in an existing code base.
Teas and coffees and a two course lunch will be included as part of the price.
 
Attendees will be expected to bring a laptop setup for C# development (either .NET or Mono stack).

description:
Strategic planning….a straight forward approach that really works!

10:00am - 12:00pm

A good strategic plan will guide an organisation towards the achievement of its mission and if you don’t have one in place your organisation will be like the proverbial ship without a rudder!

But so often strategic planning becomes overly complicated, tiring and frustrating…but it needn’t be.

This seminar will guide participants through a straightforward and highly effective process that will enable your organisation to create not only create meaningful goals but the strategies to achieve them.

 

Risk management…ignore it at your peril! 1:00pm - 3:00pm

Identifying, eliminating or reducing risk is a core responsibility of the board and senior management.

This seminar will include an explanation of the various types of risks….financial, legal, reputational, environmental, systems, program, human resource and others and how they can cause major problems and damage if they aren’t managed.

Participants will also be provided with a step by step guide that will enable them to systematically identify risks and to develop a plan to reduce or eliminate them.

Directors and Officers insurance may not provide coverage if a risk management program is not in place.

Not to be missed!

 

Good governance…what you need to know! 4:00pm - 6:00pm

Funders, government, supporters and other stakeholders are placing increasing importance on how well an organisation is governed.

This seminar has been designed for senior managers and board members who want to gain a clear understanding of the meaning of governance together with their legal and ethical responsibilities.

Participants will also receive advice and guidance on how to introduce higher standards of governance into their organisations, how to determine the split between the roles of CEO and board, and the characteristics of highly effective community service organisation boards.

description:
Introduction to Project Management full day training workshop delivered in partnership with IBM:

13 September 2013, 9.00am - 4.30pm in London South Bank, £20 per person (lunch included).
 

Workshop Information:

How many times have you had a good idea that has either failed to become a reality or, if it has, has not been delivered to everyone’s expectations? Sometimes the idea is not a great one – but more frequently the idea is great but it has not been thought through and executed very well.

The workshop will introduce participants to the basic principles and concepts of project management. The IBM team will take attendees through a series of structured activities – some in plenary, some in small groups, designed to explain why project management is a vital skill, when to use it. You’ll understand why some projects fail – and how you can minimise the risk of this happening. Participants will have an opportunity to think about how to apply a project management approach to a real project of their own, with step by step support from some of IBM’s most experienced project managers.
 

Why IBM and why these workshops?

The IBM skills workshops form one part of IBM’s commitment to the communities within which they live and work. IBM is fortunate to have large numbers of highly motivated, intelligent and capable people, along with insights and knowledge and other resources that, appropriately applied, can benefit not just large commercial and government organisations able to pay for them, but schools, charities and individuals too.
 

Who should attend?

The IBM skills workshops are targeted at staff, volunteers and trustees of small charities that are looking to improve knowledge & understanding, build confidence or develop into new areas.

The content of each of the one day workshops is based on quality resources that have been thoroughly tried and tested with charities. The workshops are delivered by teams of IBM volunteers, some of whom are subject matter experts in the topics – but all of whom are very approachable and committed to ensuring that you get the most out of your day.

The workshops very deliberately have a high level of staffing so that there are plenty of people on hand who can work with participants in small groups or individually, giving you personal and intensive coaching and support.


Location:

IBM United Kingdom Limited
76/78 Upper Ground
South Bank
London SE1 9PZ

[Directions]


Booking Information:

Please read the following before booking:

1. To get the most out of the day we recommend organisations send two representatives to the workshop. This way, having attended a workshop together there is mutual understanding and support within an organisation, to ensure that the learning is applied to real projects.

2. We usually work with a maximum of 12 organisations / 24 participants, to ensure that we can provide a high quality, high staff to learner ratio. We assign an IBM ‘buddy’ to pairs or small groups for the day, the buddy with help explain the concepts and activities.

3. We do also ask that if, having booked a place on a workshop and had that confirmed, attendees make every effort to attend – otherwise other charities miss out on the opportunity to develop their capacity and IBM volunteers running the day can end up feeling that their effort and commitment has not been worthwhile.

4. We ask each organisation / individual attending, to come to the workshop, having identified a specific project, related to the subject matter of the workshop that they wish to work on. This way the learning has a real application and a value to the organisation.

5. IBM may contact you ahead of the event so that they can better understand your organisations, the reasons for your attendance and the types of projects that you will be bringing to work on.

6. We expect participants to come prepared to fully participate in the workshops – to be open and honest about your organisation and its strengths and weaknesses, to share your expertise and ideas and to work collaboratively with other participants.


Booking Criteria:

Before you book you must be a member of the Small Charities Coalition. Membership of the Small Charities Coalition is FREE (conditions apply).

To become a member click HERE and complete the registration form. When you're done, return to this booking page.

description:
An STC Technical Editing SIG Fundraising Event

In this interactive discussion, Lori Fisher will give us her perspective on the changing role of editors as we move to a world of dynamic online content, embedded assistance, video content, and social media. She will also discuss ways to articulate the value of editing to the decision-makers in your company. 

This will be an interactive session, so bring your comments, stories, and questions! 

Speaker Profile

Lori Fisher is Director of Information Management User Technology at IBM's Silicon Valley Laboratory, leading a multi-disciplinary organization with worldwide responsibility for user experience, information development, globalization, and accessibility for the information management product portfolio in IBM's Software Group.

Lori is a leader in the corporate-wide Information Development Advisory Council and co-chair of the IBM-wide User Experience Executive Council. She developed and taught two of the core courses in a certificate program in Advanced Technical Communication at University of California Extension for almost two decades. She has served on the STC Nominating Committee, chaired the STC Quality SIG, held multiple elected positions on the local Silicon Valley STC chapter Administrative Council, and judged in various STC competitions. She served a 2-year term as Secretary of STC on the international STC Board of Directors.

Lori is a Fellow of STC in the Silicon Valley Chapter.

| Tuesdays 10 - 1 pm, Sept. 17 - Dec. 3. |

To abstract is to generalize.  This course is an appropriate follow-up to Fundamental Oils and Basic Painting.  It introduces students to a broad spectrum of abstract formats and provides an informative backdrop for stylistic approaches being practiced by working artists today.  A broad survey will commence highlighting key artists whose individual techniques reinforce the conceptual processes involved in abstract oil painting.  Studio projects will proceed in an ordered sequence to maximize technical development while introducing students to formal concerns associated with image development and colour synthesis. Upon completion, each student should possess an introductory knowledge of abstract painting that will better prepare him or her for further study in painting.  Appropriate follow-up courses include; 315 Intermediate Painting

Prerequisite:  Fundamental Oils or Introduction to Painting.

 

Instructor: Celia Neubauer  

Time: Tuesday 10 am to 1 pm

Tuition fee per term: $460 | Materials fee per term: $35


 

Materials List

 

The following colours are recommended for their versatility in providing the broadest and most effective range of colour mixing, without waste or duplication. Depending on financial resources, please endeavor to have the following:

 

Cadmium red     Alizarin crimson       Ultramarine blue       Cerulean blue

 

Cadmium yellow med.     Lemon yellow     Burnt sienna       Raw umber

 

Permanent rose or Magenta             a large tube of Titanium white

 

Solvents – Please have a large bottle of odourless solvent – Attention; no citrus solvents please.

 

Walnut oil and an alkyd medium will be distributed to the class individually.

 

Please have a large palette pad no smaller than 12 x 16 inches.

 

Supports – Please have a canvas pad & a small canvas board for the first day of class.   For the remainder of the course, specifics concerning type and size of support will vary from class to class. Please refer to the course outline for material specifics from week to week.

 

Miscellaneous

 

Please have a role of masking tape, containers with lids (jam jars work well) rags or paper towels for clean-up.

 

Brushes

 

Oil brushes – Flat #12, #6, #2

 

Oil Brushes – Round #8, #2

 

A pointed round watercolour brush #3  or #4

 

 A set of palette knives

 

Attention: Please be punctual. A talk and demonstration begins at 2:05 pm sharp.

description:
Getting older is part of a life long journey of self-discovery.

 

·        How do I make a smooth transition to becoming an older adult?

·        How do I keep my brain active and remain positive?

 

Facilitators Ava Goodman and Donald Officer dispel some nagging myths about aging well and making a smooth transition to a happier life as a senior.  This workshop is targeted for the 60 plus generation.

 

Ava Goodman examines how to keep mentally active, navigating the transitions of aging, and reconsidering the world of the senior from some interesting perspectives (social gerontology and the social determinants of aging). Age smart not hard!

 

Donald Officer explores how to apply that reactivated mind to the challenges of aging.  Find out how strategic thinking reframes tarnished mindsets and restores luster to the golden years. Start making important decisions wisely and setting attainable goals.

 

Seniors have the wisdom and the incentive to do better. Find out how to make that happen.
name: Creative Transitions for Older Adults

description:
Want your child to be active and healthy? Join us for Move, Play & Learn.

 

We are inviting children aged 18 months to 5 years to participate in our program, encouraging active play and educating you and your child on how important physical activity is at an early age.

  •  Did you know that current research is increasingly finding that children pre-school are unskilled at basic movements such as throwing, running and jumping? A recent study (Paediatrics, 2012) reported that by year 2 most children should have mastered a basic sprint, vertical jump, side gallop and leap. Unfortunately the results did not reflect this with only 10% of the sample group demonstrating all four skills.
  • Did you know that parents mistakenly believe that children naturally learn fundamental movement skills when in fact children must be taught them? Consequently, without this confidence & body familiarity, children are less likely to participate in organised or school sport or even play with their friends. Children lacking the four basic movement skills also had had lower fitness levels & were more prone to being overweight or obese. Early childhood is a critical period for the development of fundamental movement skills & studies suggest early intervention is key.


Our program will start Monday July 15 and run until Monday September 16 (inclusive)


Our program will not run on Monday August 5 and Monday September 9. You are not charged for these weeks in the term pass. 


Your order is non-refundable. All fees collected will go directly towards purchasing additional equipment.

Designed for

All educators, all service types

Summary

The National Quality Standard emphasises the value of physical environments that provide a range of safe, rich and diverse experiences which promote children’s learning and development.

Welcoming, vibrant and flexible learning environments reﬂect and enrich the lives and identities of children and families and respond to individual interests, abilities and needs. With thoughtful arrangement of spaces and resources, indoor and outdoor environments can support different levels and styles of learning and invite children and families to contribute ideas, interests and questions.

Participants will explore the connections between the indoor and outdoor environments, their influence on children’s learning and relationships and strategies for developing environmentally sustainable practices.

Learning outcomes

Part one: Making the most of the physical environment

  • Broaden knowledge of how the physical environment can influence children’s behaviour, their relationships with each other and educators, and the opportunities for self-guided learning
  • Strategies to assess and adjust the physical environment to continue to meet the needs of children and families and make the best use of indoor and outdoor environments
  • Understand the benefits to children's learning of integrated indoor and outdoor environments

Part two: Inclusive environments

  • Develop strategies to be deliberate, purposeful and thoughtful in design and organisation of the physical environment
  • Gain insights into engaging every child in experiences in the natural and built environments
  • Acquire further skills to encourage children and families to contribute ideas, interests and questions to the learning environment and how to use these to extend learning opportunities 

Part three: Environmentally sustainable practices

  • Develop strategies to plan for and promote environmentally sustainable practices
  • Gain strategies to engage children and families in environmental sustainability initiatives, and ideas for incorporating these into everyday practice
  • Deepen understandings of how to evaluate and continuously improve the effectiveness of these practices

description:
“To enjoy your life,

you need to pay attention to it”

    - Dr Craig Hassed (medical researcher with

    Monash University, author of The Essence of Health)


In this retreat we explore what it means to actually be present, to be here now in a very easy and practical way. 

Quite naturally we find that when we stop and pay attention we become more easeful, we feel open, grounded and more alive.  We rediscover and feel in to our inherent OKness.

Suitable for first timers as well as experienced meditations and mindfulness practitioners, this one day retreat is a wonderful opportunity to gift yourself some precious time just for you.


This retreat is suitable for you if you: 

  • Have never practised mindfulness or meditation or if you have attended introductory mindfulness and meditation courses and want to deepen your practise

This retreat can assist with:

  • Increasing your self-awareness and understanding.
  • Reducing the impact of negative thoughts, difficult emotions, stress, anxiety or depression
  • Relaxing more
  • Practising being mindful
  • Stimulating feelings of well-being
  • Letting go of past events

Format:

The one day retreat will consist of the following:

  • Guided mindfulness meditations
  • Guidance and instruction on mindfulness as a practice
  • Silent mindfulness meditations
  • Reflections, instructions and question and answers

 

Practical focus with no religion:

The instructions and exploration throughout the day has a focus on the practical. There are no religious or dogmatic belief systems to be adopted. The sitting meditations will be conducted in chairs. Please bring cushion or a stool with you if you prefer this.


Lunch and refreshments included:

Your registration fee includes a vegetarian lunch, refreshments as well as instructional handouts.

What is mindfulness?

Mindfulness means “paying attention in a particular way; On purpose, in the present moment, and non-judgementally.” – Jon Kabat Zinn (Professor of Medicine Emeritus Stress Reduction Clinic and the Centre for Mindfulness in Medicine).

Mindfulness is gaining in popularity as more and more people discover how this simple skill can have a profoundly positive impact on your life. Organisations such as Google, Apple, Nike and Yahoo! now run mindfulness and meditation programmes and sessions for staff during work hours.

Modern research about mindfulness and meditation shows measurable and significant benefits to people including less stress, less anxiety, greater focus, calm and happiness.

This particular retreat emphasises your own natural wisdom, your own innate OKness, right here and now. The instructions and guidance will be explicitly inviting you to embrace your whole human experience as it happens, moment by moment with a radical acceptance.

 

Refund policy and money back guarantee

Should you attend a retreat course and not be satisfied you are entitled to a  full 100% refund should you wish.

 

About the teacher:

 

Karl Baker is a director of Mindfulness Works and has been practising mindfulness and meditation for over 10 years. During that time he has worked one on one with a key meditation teacher and has attended numerous multi-day silent insight meditation retreats. Karl was involved in assisting establishing the Wellington Insight Meditation group. His principle teachers have been Stephen (Nyanaviro) Archer, Shard Rogell, Jeremy Logan and now Sri Guru Yanchiji.

Karl has as honours degree from Victoria University and has helped found 3 successful businesses.

Karl’s approach is straight forward, practical, heartfelt and directed towards you discovering your own innate wisdom and authentic experience.

 

“I had never done meditation before and already had preconceived notions of what it would be like such as “religious and a bit airy fairy”. Surprisingly this course was the opposite. I found Karl very relatable, when he talked about our thoughts. Like a lot of people, I tend to overthink everything from past events to future, or simply beating myself up. Karl helped me to take a step back and recognise I’m not my negative thoughts and they do not define me. I now feel a sense of peace. The mediation itself is relaxing and helps you de-stress from the day’s events. I highly recommend this course to anyone who is looking to de-stress and gain inner peace.” - Summer Mills

description:
SH&BA CONSUMER PANEL MEETING

Date: Thursday 25th July 2013 – 14.00 to 17.00hrs

Venue:  To be confirmed, Westminster, London SW1P

Chair:  Zoe McLeod – Consumer Focus

AGENDA

  • Welcome and Introductions
  • Review of notes from meeting held in May
  • Actions.(see action list in notes from previous meeting)
  • SH&BA overview & update from other panels
  • Creation of sub groups, working groups to carry out Actions
  1. Landscaping Group
  2. Manufacturers/Designers Group
  3. Technology Trends Group. To develop perspectives on technology trends that will affect consumers, both beneficially and otherwise. Output will be documents with differing perspectives:  1. perhaps for policy makers, 2. for consumers, 3. for industry.
  4. NFP interface Group; with remit to widen the awareness of and input into the Panel and aim that consumer facing groups hold joint understandings of specific issues.
  5. Governmental and Parliamentary Interface group.
  6. Consumer psychology and economics – It is probably almost as important as enabling a two way discussion of what drives people to purchase or use services in terms of both economics and psychology.
  • Major areas of interest, Gaps and Panel policies – Round table discussion
  • Areas where we can deliver value and change – Round table discussion
  • Terms of Reference and objectives of the Panel
  • Proposed programme for the year.

             a. Outline Calendar - Date of next meetings: 25th July, SP suggests 17th                          September, 20th November 20th
             b. Plan meetings for specific issues
             c. Planning a conference in Autumn in conjunction with Consumer Futures
             d. SH&BA News – IOT-Bay project, IOT Interoperability

  • Actions and timescales for the above
    1. Action List
  • Close

 

SH&BA is very aware that the consumers as end users to all products for people in the built environment are important and understanding what consumers want, need and actually get is a vital consideration for developers of products, service providers and thus SH&BA members.


The Consumer Panel is part of a feedback (and feed forward) loop that is intended to assist SH&BA members make strategic policy decisions, assist in directing Research Policies by Government, TSB and University (members) and lastly to help people using products to understand what is available, why they might use them and keep them informed of what could be their best choice in buying products and services.


The Consumer Panel will be slightly different from the other Panels as it will work to ensure the consumer perspective is made apparent to the other panels and by extension work that they initiate in the WGs. This will be a two way process and the panel will also inform consumer facing organisations and consumers about advances and opportunities in technical, product and service areas. It may commission informational literature and communicate via social media into a consumer audience.


The Consumer Panel will have a general and specific role. It will meet to hold meetings to understand consumer related issues and it is expected that these will highlight particular issues in various sectors that will require special attention. There will thus be meetings held to cover such issues.


It is intended that the Consumer Panel will be headed up by people from consumer groups with support fron the SH&BA secretariat and that its membership will be representative of all the other Panels and WGs of SH&BA.

MISSION

To grow the market for smart products and services for people at home, in buildings and communities through the exchange of information and knowledge and by involvement in new projects and business opportunities.

OBJECTIVES

The objective of SHABA is to grow the market throughout the Smart Built Environment for systems that deliver useful services to people. SHABA will have four major areas of activity:

  • To inform and build the input of smart electronic systems and services throughout the built environment in homes, buildings and in cities.
  • To ensure that people understand the value and benefit of these products and services and to interface far more strongly with people both directly and through consumer organisations to seek the views of users to identify the good and the bad points of the services and products and gaps in the market.
  • To ensure that these smart systems in all sectors of the home, buildings and the future city can work together interoperably and thus provide people with the best possible experience of living in the new connected digital environment.
  • To engage with research and development organisations in UK and Europe and facilitate knowledge exchange at all levels for the benefit of members and create a knowledge repository.

Aanmelden kan tot 1 september a.s. Na aanmelding en betaling kun je nog tot 1 september a.s. je inschrijving annuleren, dan wordt het inschrijvingsbedrag teruggestort. Doelstelling is om alle ex-Digital medewerkers in Nederland te benaderen, maar wellicht weten wij niet iedereen te bereiken. Dus: Spread the word!

We hopen jullie allemaal te zien!

description:
INTRODUCTORY LEVEL

| Thursdays 10 - 1 pm, Oct. 24 - Nov. 28. |

This course will provide a fundamental approach to watercolour, for both the beginner and advanced student, with an emphasis on transparency, colour mixing, brushworks, washes and illumination while being true to the John Singer Sargent approach to the medium. Students will work from still-life and landscape and can expect demonstrations followed by ample painting time, and a critique towards the end of each class.  All levels welcome.

Please note this class is 6 weeks in duration (Oct. 24 – Nov. 28)

 

Instructor: Brian Hoxha

Time: Thursday 10 am – 1 pm

Tuition fee per term: $275 |  Model fee per term: $20


 

Materials List

 

COLOURS  

  • Titanium white (winsor Newton), cadmium yellow light, cadmium orange, yellow ochre, cadmium scarlet, cadmium red deep, Permanent Rose (WN) Alizarin Crimson, burnt sienna, sepia, Winsor green /Blue shade, Paynes Gray, Winsor violet (dioxazine violet), French ultra marine blue, Winsor  blue red/shade, cobalt blue, maganese blue, Cobalt Turquoise Pale (Winsor & Newton), cerulean blue, indigo blue. Recommended tube paints: Winsor & Newton, Holbein, M. Graham Co. Stevensons all in 15ml watercolours 

 ***An alternative to Holbein’s Cadmium Green Pale is the M.Graham Company’s Permanent Green Pale. 

 

BRUSHES 

  • # 12 - 24 Round synthetic sable 
  • #   6 Round synthetic sable 
  • 1/4 to 1" flat synthetic sable 
  • # 2 Rigger brush synthetic sable 
  • An assortment of Chinese watercolour brushes can be used instead 

 

PAPER 

  • 140 pound Arches Watercolour paper s/m/rough 
  • 300 pound smooth, hot pressed paper, and 300 pound rough 

  

PALETTES 

  • Any plastic, ceramic or metal palette with a ridged reservoir mixing, and enough slots for all the colours listed would be suitable. Recommended palette: Robert E. Wood 24 pan palette (cheapest at Gwartzman's) John Pike Palette 20 pan (can only be found at Curry's) 

 

BOARDS 

  • There is an assortment of boards under the cupboard in the sink area. 

 

Additional Materials 

  • Sponges (natural or industrial), tissue or paper toweling, razor blades, titanium white (WN),  calligraphy knibs, masking fluid, HB pencils, gum erasers.
name: 629 Introduction to Watercolour (F'13) - Brian Hoxha

Deskripsi :
“River Scapes In Flux” adalah pameran seni rupa internasional mengenai lingkungan hidup dan kebudayaan bentang sungai di Asia Tenggara.
The art project “Riverscapes IN FLUX”, conceptualized and initiated by the Goethe-Institut Vietnam, seeks to create a discourse on this ecological key issue in a new context. The Goethe-Institut invited young artists from Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Myanmar, Indonesia and the Philippines to reflect the ecological as well as socio-economic and cultural changes that the riverscapes in these countries are currently experiencing in their work. 17 art works have been created: Multimedia installations and photo series, videos and object installations. The exhibition “Riverscapes IN FLUX” has been shown in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh (Vietnam), Bangkok (Thailand), Phnom Penh (Cambodia) and Manila (The Philippines).
For Indonesia, the Goethe-Institut has chosen Langgeng Art Foundation, Yogyakarta as exhibition venue. As in the previous setups, this exhibition will be completed by a range of cultural and educational activities, such as film screenings, guided tours through the exhibition with the curator, as well as discussions with the artists involved and environmental experts.
