From his 2011 #1 hit “Reboot,” which spent 7 weeks at #1 on Beatport, to this recent genre-­‐defying #1 smash hit “The Box” – one of the most played records at EDC Las Vegas 2012 – Ummet continues to surge in popularity worldwide.

Beginning with his first hits “Time Wave Zero” (Doorn Records), “Arcadia” (Doorn Records) and Shamballa (Reset), Ummet showed the world that he had something different to offer…and the top names in the industry are quickly joined his huge global fan base.

In 2012 he landed a collaboration with Paul van Dyk and together they’ve produced a track called ‘Dae Yor’ for Paul van Dyk’s album ‘Evolution’. As a Dj he is in high demand and is playing the international field and high ranked clubs and festivals like Godskitchen, Pacha, Eden, Mondaybar, Tomorrowland, Planet Love, Global Gathering, A State of Trance etc.
Continuously garnering huge support from a broad array of the world’s top jocks like Armin van Buuren, David Guetta, Avicii, and Sander van Doorn, Ummet Ozcan is firming his position at the forefront of the next generation of brilliant EDM Producers.

With an unprecedented amount of artists seeking the formula for club-­‐friendly absolution, Revealed Recordings proudly premiered their first secret weapon of the New Year -­‐-­‐ W&W and Ummet Ozcan’s ‘The Code’. It entered at #1 in the DMC buzz chart. ‘The Code’ has been one of the tracks with the biggest buzz around for months. It is currently #1 in the main Beatport chart.

Ummet is also known for his softsynth and soundbank design for well established music software houses like Rob Papen (Albino, Predator) and Acces Music (Virus).

At this moment he is developing a new synthesizer along with new spectacular unheard of sounds that will definitely pave the way for a fresh new musical breeze thru EDM. description:
FOOD CAN CHANGE YOUR LIFE IN UNEXPECTED WAYS.

What if you could increase your energy, sleep better, improve athletic performance, and lose weight--permanently?

What if you could break the unhealthy cycle of food cravings, indulgence, and guilt--forever?

What if you could stop dieting and start living a healthier lifestyle--effortlessly, without feeling like you are missing out on anything?

And what if you could eliminate the symptoms of your medical condition--just by changing the food you put on your plate?


"The Whole9 Nutrition Seminar is one of the best classes I have attended on nutrition--ever." -Dr. Daniel Kalish, founder, The Kalish Method


THE AUTHORS OF IT STARTS WITH FOOD WILL SHOW YOU HOW.

Join Sarah Ramsden and Summer Innanen of Whole9 (the creators of the original Whole30® Program) for an interactive, un-complicated, fun (really!) seminar designed to teach you everything you need to know about creating a life-long, healthy relationship with food (and say "no" to diets forever).


In a 2011 survey of more than 2,000 Whole9 nutrition plan followers, more than 95% lost weight or improved body composition...without ever thinking about weight loss!


AT OUR EVENT, YOU'LL LEARN...

How foods in today’s modern world affect us psychologically, leading to cravings, addictions, and the cycle of guilt, shame, and remorse, and how stress impacts this process.

How a healthy metabolism works in the body, and how certain foods promote metabolic dysfunction (related to blood sugar management, insulin resistance, leptin resistance, and cortisol resistance).

The principles of basic digestion, the importance of maintaining a healthy digestive tract, which foods can compromise digestion, and the effect on all body systems.

How to identify chronic systemic inflammation, how certain foods stimulate immune activity in the body, and the relationship between food and lifestyle-related diseases and conditions.

Which food choices make you healthier, promoting a healthy metabolism and reducing inflammation.

How to plan meals and pre- and post-workout fueling to maximize nutrition and promote optimal health and fitness in a way that feels effortless and sustainable.

To recognize the difference between fueling and training for health versus performance, and be able to apply your own personalized strategies to meet your goals.

A basic understanding of how sleep, stress, exercise, recovery, and other lifestyle factors impact your overall health (in conjunction with nutrition).

Exactly how to discover your own personalized, optimized diet by following our 30-day program.


“I have been a lifelong acute asthmatic.  Hundreds of ER visits, hospitalizations and so forth.  I would normally have to take 4-5 control medications, and my inhaler multiple times a day. Since I began the Whole30 on October 4th, 2012, I have been un-medicated for the first time in my life. It is something miraculous to feel life as you have never known it.” Andrea B., Minneapolis, MN

 

SEMINAR DETAILS

Seminars run from 9 AM - 4 PM, with a one-hour lunch break. Some events are catered (for a small fee); for the rest we encourage you to bring your own lunch and spend your break socializing with the presenters and your fellow attendees.

With your registration fee, you'll also receive a packet full of resources, recipes, meal planning tools, and special discounts. We'll also give you samples of some Whole30® Approved products we love!


With the Whole30, I was able to identify and eliminate which foods were causing me so much trouble. I lost weight in areas of my body that were difficult for years to shed. I can wear the jeans that I hid away 3 years ago! The Whole30 is a lifestyle for me now – I feel like I have finally found a program that works." -Catherine H., Albuquerque, NM

Rupert talks – to audiences as diverse as Google management and Special Forces soldiers – are inspiring, funny and challenging. His expeditions provide a spectacular, original case study of self-motivation, setting small targets to achieve outrageous goals, the rewards of risk and teamwork, the power of story-telling, overcoming difficult times and self-doubt, the magnificence of our world, and a call to arms that nothing is achieved without being bold enough to begin it. The lessons from the road.

As well as the major adventures, Rupert’s award-winning concept of microadventures -short, adventurous journeys close to home- encourage people to take practical steps to challenge themselves by undertaking adventures of their own and improving their physical health, mental well-being, and all-important work/life balance

 

Rupert has presented to audiences on six continents, speaking for hundreds of schools, the Royal Geographical Society, TEDx, England Rugby, the British Army and corporate clients including Google, Ernst & Young, BP, T-Mobile and Nokia.

 

He has been selected as one of National Geographic’s Adventurers of the Year.

With over 20 years under ourbelt, our career spans all aspects of the industry. we have worked at Madame Tussauds, theNatural History Museum and First Protocol (event marketing and management). In that time he came across thousands of staff.

 

‘Sometimes the quality was excellent and it was clear that lots of effort had been put into the recruitment process. Other times, the standard wasn’t that good. Staff were sent from agencies, they didn’t know who the client was, the uniform wasn’t there and they didn’t have the skills or engagement.’

 

In 2001, motivated by a desire to provide a better offering, he launched Off to Work. The company provides a wide range of staff for events and has worked at the Brits, ELLE Awards, Test matches at Lords, England football internationals at Wembley and a host of arena concerts. ‘We work at the top end of the industry. For our clients, cost does matter, but quality is more important.’

 

The company is divided into four distinct areas: People, Training, Consultancy and Platinum. In terms of its staff, it is the sheer variety that is the first point of note – from mixologists and flaring bartenders to back of house chefs and toilet attendants.

 

Training is a central part of the company’s operation. ‘You have to invest a huge amount to make sure the team is going to do the right thing when they are out there.’ The business has its own dedicated training team and a number of centres across the UK. The latest of these ‘academies’ opened at the London Irish Centre in 2011. Courses range from straightforward food safety awareness and first aid to more specialist skills such as barista and cocktail bar training, and wine education.

 

A consultancy for clients looking for permanent staff is another of the Atkins’ services. Besides full-time appointments advertised online, the company organises Reverse Recruitment evenings where clients get the chance to meet candidates.

org_desc:
The Jazzschool is an innovative nonprofit organization dedicated to the study and performance of jazz — America’s indigenous art form —and related styles of music from around the world. Founded in 1997, the Jazzschool is located in the historic Kress Building at Shattuck and Addison, in the heart of the Downtown Berkeley Arts District. The Jazzschool is part of a vibrant East Bay arts community that includes the Freight & Salvage, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, Aurora Theatre, East Bay Media Center and renowned Cal Performances at the University of California.

Hailed as one of the nation’s most comprehensive centers for jazz studies, the Jazzschool offers instrumentalists and vocalists of all ages and skill levels a broad spectrum of performance ensembles, lectures, workshops and private instruction. Courses are designed for the professional musician, the serious student and the jazz aficionado seeking personal enrichment. A multi-faceted institution, the Jazzschool comprises several key components.

Jazzschool Institute

The Jazzschool Institute is a music conservatory offering the aspiring professional a comprehensive 4-year degree program culminating in the Bachelor of Music in Jazz Studies. The Institute provides a challenging curriculum of performance, jazz theory and improvisation, ear training, composition, arranging, transcription and analysis, and music history courses, taught by professional artists and educators. Coursework also includes music business, music technology and financial planning, thoroughly preparing students for a fulfilling career in the performing arts.

Jazzschool Community Music School (JCMS)

The JCMS provides music education and performance opportunities for people of all ages and levels of ability. Consisting of the JCMS Adult Music Program and the JCMS Young Musicians Program, the JCMS operates year-round on a quarterly basis and offers over 100 ensembles, courses and workshops to build all aspects of musicianship. Students are routinely featured in concert performances, open to the public. With a formidable faculty of renowned musicians and educators, the JCMS is a cornerstone of the Bay Area’s thriving music scene.

JCMS ADULT MUSIC PROGRAM

The Jazzschool Adult Music Program offers life-enriching opportunities to learn about and play jazz and related styles of music from throughout the world. Courses are available for both instrumentalists and vocalists, and everyone from young adult to senior citizen is welcome. Instruction and performances occur primarily in late afternoons, evenings and on weekends, making the program easily accessible to the working professional.

JCMS YOUNG MUSICIANS PROGRAM

The Jazzschool Young Musicians Program offers middle and high school students of all skill levels a wide variety of combos, big bands and vocal performance courses throughout the entire year, as well as camps during the summer. Select ensembles participate in national competitions, and Jazzschool bands have routinely taken top awards from DownBeat, the Monterey Next Generation Jazz Festival and others.

Workshops

Visiting artists and Jazzschool faculty lead fascinating and practical workshops, typically a single session of two or three hours in length and held on a Sunday. Content may focus on any specific aspect of jazz theory or performance, such as playing in odd time signatures or the art of vocal improvisation. Past workshops have been taught by prominent musicians from Bobby McFerrin to Dave Liebman, Janis Siegel, Peter Erskine, Sheila Jordan, Nguyên Lê and others.

Concerts

The Jazzschool facility includes an intimate venue with seating capacity of 100. Throughout the year, Jazzschool faculty and students perform for the public, providing a real-world incubator for developing new concepts and gaining audience exposure in the competitive Bay Area environment. High-profile artists have performed at the Jazzschool, including Terence Blanchard, Art Lande, Kim Nalley, Taylor Eigsti, Sachal Vasandani and many more.

Jazzschool Books & Records

The Jazzschool’s in-house retail store is a treasure trove of jazz-related reading and listening materials. It provides students, teachers and the public with convenient access to extraordinary books, recordings, videos and accessories.

Jazzcaffè

Located within the Jazzschool facility, the Jazzcaffè serves up delectable fare for students and visitors to enjoy a convenient bite to eat. A changing menu features house-made soups, salads and sandwiches, as well as beer, wine, espresso and desserts. Drop by for a great meal to match the great music!

Transportation

The Jazzschool is easily accessible by car and public transportation. The downtown Berkeley BART station and AC Transit bus stops are within a block. There is a public parking garage just a few steps away on Addison, in addition to metered street parking throughout the neighborhood.

 

REFUND POLICY
Registration fees and first class tuition for classes are non-refundable. Requests to drop must be received in writing within 48 hours of the first class meeting in order to qualify for a refund; please visit the main office or e-mail drop@jazzschool.org to request a refund. Refunds for remaining tuition are not possible after the 48-hour drop deadline.

$100 per week of camp tuition is non-refundable; the remainder is refundable only until the cancellation deadline (see program information). Refunds are not possible after the cancellation deadline.

Tuition for intensives, workshops and short-term classes is non-refundable.

Exceptions may be granted only in the case of extremely serious medical or family emergencies; please enclose a doctor’s note and/or other supplementary documentation with your request. Please note that refunds will not be granted for classes dropped due to scheduling conflicts arising after the start of the session.

Please note: Refunds make take up to 30 days to process.

TICKETS SALES
All ticket sales are final. Refunds or exchanges are not possible.

Concert and workshop tickets are available online at By phone (Toll Free):1-866-384-3060 Monday–Friday 9am – 5pm
In Person at the Jazzschool, 2087 Addison Street, Berkeley. Monday – Saturday 10am – 5:30pm, Sundays 11am – 3pm
For more information please call the Jazzschool at (510) 845-5373

All concerts are $5 for students enrolled in the Jazzschool Young Musicians Program. Purchase a package of 5 or more concerts and receive a 20% discount!

All concerts are $5 for youth under 12. Discounted tickets available to seniors (65+) and students with valid ID.
Ticketing Policies: All ticket sales are final. Refunds or exchanges are not possible.

SEATING POLICY
Performances start promptly at the published time. Doors open 30 minutes  prior to performances. Seating is “open” and available on a first-come, first-served basis.
Please note: an advance sale ticket does NOT guarantee late comers a seat. Late comers may be asked to wait in the lobby until intermission or an appropriate interval to be seated.

EMAIL POLICY
Information collected by the mailing list form is used solely for the purpose of notifying you of Jazzschool events or related information that might interest you. We have no intent to sell or otherwise distribute your e-mail address and/or information to any other entity.

description:
About Stuart Bakewell

Stuart has worked in the voluntary sector for over 20 years, and currently works as an Area Manager for St Mungo’s, a large homelessness charity based in London and the South West of England. He has a professional background in providing mental health services, and is also a qualified auricular acupuncturist.

His current work involves staff and service development, strategic planning and management responsibility for a wide range of supported housing services. Stuart has played a lead role in the adoption and implementation of recovery based practice within the organisation, and recently in establishing St Mungo’s Recovery College, which provides a range of educational and learning opportunities to clients, staff, volunteers and also to the wider community.  

Stuart is passionate about improving service delivery across the sector.  He has actively contributed to policy development and innovation, and advocates widely for systemic change.

Richmond Fellowship WA and Arafmi proudly present this unique training opportunity with Stuart Bakewell.

 

Using the Outcomes Star to Improve Services

The Outcomes Star can be used to help people evaluate their skills and competencies and track their progress over time. It can also help to identify what successful change will look like, enabling the celebration of success and increasing people’s understanding of areas which need more work.

Using the Outcomes Star can also be a great value in evidencing an organisation’s work, providing support for funding applications, along with information to inform reports to commissioners, service reviews, quality assurance and improving client involvement.

Learning Outcomes:
On completion of this course you will:

  • Appreciate what the Outcomes Star system can do, and how it can help to improve services
  • Understand how the Star may be used in key working sessions
  • Have the ability to use the Star to identify both the individual and wider impacts of your organisation

This course would be suitable for:
Anyone interested in this topic including, but not limited to:

  • Consumers
  • Carers
  • Interested family, friends and community members
  • Students
  • Service providers including
  • Recovery and social workers
  • Mental health professionals
  • Alcohol and drug workers
  • Justice workers
  • Sexual health workers

 

For more information about this course, please visit our website at www.rfwa.org.au

Other courses by this facilitator

Join us for a delicious two whole days immersed in The Lovechefs craft and take home some of the secrets of a vibrant, living, loving kitchen.


 

This weekend is designed to pass on some key techniques and ideas for you to combine with your existing kitchen routine to help the cultivation of friendly bacteria and good habits in your life!

Friendly fire: We're particularly excited about fermented foods at the moment and will be showing and sharing some different sauerkraut, kombucha and keffir recipes and techniques. Friendly digestive bacteria are essential for your mental and physical health and home-made fermented foods are the way forward.

 

Friendly sweet: Refined, gourmet cakes, fools, mousses and tortes without dairy, eggs, wheat or sugar. Eliminating refined sugar is also central in restoring friendly bacteria and to giving you increasing control over your mental patterns and behaviour. We'll share the key techniques to making the world's tastiest sweets that are also the healthiest.


 

Friendly protein: Proteinous, enzymatic pates and probiotic cheeses using sprouted seeds and nuts. Open up a new range of satisfying protein options with techniques for seasoning your own inventions to create endless possibilities.

Martijn Sjoorda

Martijn is sinds zijn jeugd gefascineerd hoe relaties tussen mensen werken, of beter gezegd niet werken. David Ogilvy, de vader van de strategische marketing heeft hier een grote invloed in gehad. Vooral waar het gaat om visievorming en ondernemerschap.

Martijn richt zich op de menselijke dynamiek van verandering, met een scherp oog voor brede strategische vraagstukken. Als zelfstandig adviseur en trainer, werkt hij intensief met het levensveranderende werk van Dr. David Kantor, meester gezinstherapeut.

Tijdens het werken met grote corporate cliënten zoals Unilever, Nuon, Lucent & Deloitte, heeft hij een methode ontwikkeld die op het snijvlak van dialoog, strategie, leiding geven en execute organisaties helpt beter te presteren. Martijn spreekt zes talen en werkt in het Nederlands, het Engels, het Duits, het Frans, het Spaans en het Italiaans.

Martijn behaalde een BBA in Rotterdam en werd opgeleid door Peter Senge, Bill Isaacs et al., David Kantor en is gecertificeerd in Systemisch Werken (Phoenix), diverse andere psychotherapeutische scholen en SOQ en MSP. Hij is getrouwd en vader van 3 kinderen. Hij houdt van lezen, schrijven fotografie, wandelen, koken en kunst. Hij ondersteunt actief diverse goede doelen.

Hanneke Muijs

Hanneke begon haar loopbaan als HR consultant bij Ernst & Young. Daar verdiepte ze zich, mede door een post HBO Strategisch HRM, in de toepasbaarheid van HR instrumenten in de praktijk.
 
Later, als Senior HR Adviseur bij Fortis kreeg ze de kans een opleiding tot coach te doen bij dé coachopleiding van Nederland, School voor Coaching. Toen ze haar klus - begeleiding bij de sluiting van een bedrijfsonderdeel van Fortis - had afgerond stapte ze over naar a.s.r. verzekeringen waar ze als trainer werkte met teams van elk niveau in het verbeteren van hun effectiviteit. Daar deed ze ook een uitgebreide opleiding voor. 
 
Tevens is Hanneke sinds 10 jaar trainer en supervisor op de Hogeschool van Utrecht.
Haar stijl kenmerkt zich door hoge resultaatgerichtheid en het maken van échte verbinding met deelnemers.
Binnen why* consulting is Hanneke met name bezig met het verhogen van effectiviteit en het verlagen van de feedbackdrempel in teams. 
 
Hanneke is getrouwd en heeft drie kinderen. Ze sport graag en veel en houdt van zeilen en uitgebreid koken voor vrienden.

description:
6heads Summer Walk: Vitsoe & Design for Longevity

Join 6heads on Sunday July 14th for a day exploring the beautiful coastline of Dover on foot with like-minded sustainability practitioners.  It's just a short train-ride from London St Pancras. Enjoy some delicious local food at the lunchtime pub, while being inspired by a thought-provoking talk about design for longevity by Geof Howe from Vitsoe.  All you need to do to secure your place is to pre-pay for your train tickets below (£22 per person).
 
The plan for the day is to meet at 9:30am in St.Pancras Station at Sourced Market (under the departure/arrivals board in the central concourse opposite Starbucks). We'll take the high speed train for a 69 minute journey to Dover Priory station.
 
We'll then set off on what Walks Near London describes as "one of the finest walks in England". There should be stunning views of the English Channel and, if there's good visibility, of the French coast from Boulogne to Dunkirk. The walk is surprisingly level or gently undulating for most of the way with two main climbs, out of Dover at the start of the walk and out of St.Margeret's Bay after lunch. The lunchtime stop is The Coastguard Pub, where Geof Howe from Vitsoe will give a short talk about desiging for longevity. If you google "Good Design" the first result is a link to the Vitsoe website and its Founder, Dieter Rams' 10 Principles for Good Design. What better business to speak about better, longer-lasting design as a vital aspect of more sustainable business and how Vitsoe has brought this philosophy to life through its approach to design, manufacturing and customer service?
 

After lunch we follow a tranquil coastal path behind the pebble beaches of Deal, passing Walmer Castle and Deal Castle. There's an option to stop for tea at the end of Deal pier, before returning by train to London. The total walking time should be about five hours meaning that we should be back to London for about 7pm, allowing time for lunch.
Places are very limited due to the capacity of the lunchtime pub, so we're asking you to secure your place by pre-paying for your train ticket. This allows us to get half-price groupsave tickets. The total cost you need to pre-pay for the return train ticket is £22.
We expect good weather, but do check the weather forecast before the walk and bring waterproofs if rain is forecast. You'll need footwear that is comfortable and that has a good grip. Comfortable, sturdy running shoes should be ok if the weather is dry. If rain is forecast, consider hiking boots or comfortable wellingtons.
 
Hope you can join us!
 
Regards,
The 6heads
 
For any queries or if you want more info please contact James Payne on 07803857018 or at james.payne@6-heads.com
 
6-heads.com
name: Steps Towards Sustainability - Vitsoe & Design for Longevity

Two years after John announced on our honeymoon that he wanted to quit his job and "do something in cheese," we unlocked the front door to our very own cheese shop on February 11, 2010. We've been asked many times since, "Why a Cheese Shop?" and the answer is simple. After putting ourselves through cheese bootcamps, running a cheese club out of our house, attending cheese conferences, interning for French affineur Herve Mons, journeying through Europe, and eating our way through thousands of tasty cheese morsels, we honed in on our true passions: eating, talking, traveling, and spending time together. Over a bottle of wine one evening, we realized that working behind a cheese case would bring them all together.

Ignoring all evidence of a down economy we went for it. The result is our cheese shop where we focus on sourcing the finest artisanal cheese and providing cut to order service in a relaxed, "taste before you buy" environment. Nestled into historic Hyde Park, our business has since grown to include a Cheese House. While the Cheese Shop remains our dedicated retail space, our Cheese House, located directly across the street, allows us to better serve the growing demand by our restaurant partners and customers for more cheese education.

While you're visiting our website, you'll find many photos of the products we offer. Unfortunately you can't taste them through your screen. So come by the shop and let our passionate team of cheesemongers do what they do best: guide you through the case sharing the stories of their favorite products and offering small tastes to make you smile. We hope to see you soon.

~ John and Kendall Antonelli

description:
The Smart Transport Research Centre (STRC) was established in 2011 as a research partnership between industry, government (TMR & QML) and academia. The three research themes of STRC are Simulation, visualisation and modeling; Managed Motorways and Real time Traveller Information. In this first part of this presentation, Edward Chung will give an overview and outcomes of STRC research activities. He will present the Model Free Network coding, use of Bluetooth MAC address data, Motorway control and Area Network control. Ashish Bhaskar will give the second part of the presentation on Real Time and Predictive Traveller Information where he will present the technical details including:

a)      Travel time estimation on motorways using loops only

b)      Modelling Bluetooth and fusion with loops

c)       Overview of the Multimodal trip planner.

 Prof. Edward Chung is the inaugural Director of Smart Transport Research Centre and Professor of Intelligent Transport Systems at Queensland University of Technology. He is also a visiting professor at the Advanced Mobility Research Centre (ITS Centre) located at the University of Tokyo. Earlier, he was the Head of the ITS group at Traffic facilities laboratory at Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, Lausanne in Switzerland. Edward’s practical experience includes several EU-funded projects including: Intelligent Roads; real-time monitoring, surveillance and control of road networks under adverse weather conditions; and as task leader on the Network of Excellence for Advanced Road Cooperative Traffic management in the Information Society.

 Ashish Bhaskar is the research domain leader at Smart Transport Research Centre and a lecturer at Queensland University of Technology (QUT). Before joining QUT, he did his PhD and Post-doc from EPFL, Switzerland and Masters in Transport Engineering from University of Tokyo, Japan and undergraduate in Civil Engineering from Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur India. Currently, he is focusing on the development of innovative algorithms using loops and Bluetooth for real time and predictive traveller information systems. The algorithms will be integrated in a multimodal trip planner with case studies on the Brisbane network.
name: AGM & STRC Program Overview

2nd Annual Mobile Apps 2013 To be held on 30th August 2013 at Matthan Hotel, Bangalore, India
 
 The global mobile industry is witnessing volatile growth for last couple of years. Advancement of mobile technology, improved infrastructure and Smartphone revolution have allowed people to perform much more with their mobile phones than ever before. This has resulted in an exponential demand and growth of mobile applications.
 
 The mobile app market is thriving to great heights. More than hundreds of handsets are capable of installing and running apps and a swerve of big-name app stores are striving to compete. It is expected that the market for mobile applications will be "as big as the internet", peaking at 10 million apps in 2020.
 
 Presently India having over 800+ million mobile connections and 50-150m mobile internet users it is evident mobile apps are becoming very popular. By 2015 India is expected to have 237 million mobile internet “activated” connections. Entrepreneurs are focusing a lot on mobile apps which are internet rather than SMS based. Mobile App Stats in India - 100 million apps being downloaded in India every month. India’s app developer base is estimated at 250,000.
 
 With world’s foremost brands recognizing the need of their presence in at least one of the top applications stores and the average mobile application per brand rising over 25 (for top 100 brands, 250 in case of media companies globally); the mobile applications market has took new role in defining the marketing strategy of businesses. This has opened up new horizons for already booming mobile applications market and provides faster acceleration for the market. Though these global brands do not look to make money directly with apps; however, the apps are adding up their brand equity. description:
Building on KREOD’s success at the London 2012 Olympic Games and Blackbridge Cross Borders growing success facilitating Foreign Direct Investment in the UK and China, award-winning architectural designer and Managing Director of KREOD, Chun Qing Li, and Chairman of Blackbridge, Alexander Jarvis, have now signed an exciting partnership agreement that will represent a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for entrepreneurs and investors to have their brand at the heart of one of the biggest cultural spectacles on Earth. As part of the upcoming Olympic Games in 2016, this partnership will bring to Rio de Janeiro a trade pavilion seven times larger in size than that seen in London. The Game’s slogan: “Viva sua Paixão”, means “Live Your Passion” and it is this pivotal sporting event in Brazil that will allow the Brazilian people to do just that. KREOD’s involvement will help present real opportunities for economic growth and prosperity from which a combined population of 1.6 billion people in Brazil, China and the United Kingdom can only benefit.

As a 300 Sq.m fully functioning structure, the KREOD International Trade Pavilion will allow entrepreneurs and industry leaders to showcase the world’s most innovative products and services on a totally unique events platform. Through an ambitious programme of cross-sector International business events during August and September 2016, the project will assist in accelerating economic growth throughout the participating countries involved.

Taking place on the 12th of September at the prestigious Hilton Hotel in Mayfair, the KREOD London Launch is one of the most exclusive events of the 2013 business calendar. It will provide the opportunity for over 200 business leaders, decision makers and successful individuals to discuss the future of business for Brazil, the United Kingdom and China. At this event, KREOD founder, Chun Qing Li, whose design won the famed Surface Design Awards earlier this year, and Blackbridge Chairman, Alexander Jarvis, whose private, trans-global organisation focuses on structuring, advising and facilitating arbitrages, foreign direct investment and raising capital across the world, will be revealing the design plans of this visionary initiative. They will also discuss in further detail the mission, purpose, and vast number of opportunities available for KREOD’s associates and benefactors. Visitors will then have the opportunity to network with the eclectic mix of industry professionals that will be working on the KREOD project and as part of its trade mission.

 

Event overview:

Date: Thursday, 12th September 2013
Time: 17:30 - 20:00
Venue: 22 Park Lane London W1K 1BE UK London
Dress Code: International business attire

Programme:

17:30 Receptions/Networking
18:20 Welcome Address, Mr Alexander Jarvis, Chairman & CEO, Blackbridge
18:25 Address, Mr Chun Qing Li, Managing Director of KREOD & Pavilion Architecture
18:30 Address, Mr Flavio Marega, Minister Counsellor. Embassy of Brazil in London
18:40 Address, Sir Peter Heap KCMG. Former British Ambassador to Brazil
18:45 Networking
20:00 End of formal proceedings


Delegates from the organizations listed will be in attendance at the KREOD launch:
Ramboll, Pavilion Architecture, Coutts, People's Daily Online UK, Embassy of Brazil in London, Ministry of Commerce PROC Russia & UK, Bank of China, UBS, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer, Taylor Fordyce, Phoenix TV, Olswang, North Square Blue Oak Bank, Ivanhoe Cambridge Group, Clemetsdale Group, Reneport, Royal Garden Hotel, 11 Stone Buildings, Res Europa, Interactive media Britain, China Britain Business Council, Urbanista, Thomson Reuters, Rio Negocios, Wyn River, Urban Cloud Network, International Business and Diplomatic Exchange, Baker Tilly, GCC, Bell Pottinger Private, Nee Hao Magazine, Sing Tao Daily, China UK Gateway, Bentley UK, Braskem, Caldeira UK, Carlyle Group (China), Carlyle Group (Singapore), CBRE Real Estate, China In Africa, China Merchants Property, Kuwait Finance House, Masraf Al Rayan, Saudi Arabian Mining, Uralkali, VankeCappelle Architects, Wikistrat and World Architecture News.


Sponsors:


Limited tickets available.

Official Twitter hashtag: #KREOD2016Rioproject BCB KREOD


Speakers,

 Alexander SW. Jarvis

Chairman of Blackbridge Cross Borders (BCB) - a private, trans-global organization that focuses on structuring, advising and facilitating arbitrages, Foreign Direct Investment, and raising capital on a global scale. Alexander, in partnership with Chun Qing Li, holds the position of CIO at KREOD and will be heading the project’s commercial arm for the 2016 Rio project.


Chun Qing Li

Chun Qing Li (AKA Lee) is an entrepreneur, award winning architectural designer, managing director of KREOD. He has spearheaded the design, finance, build and creation of KREOD Pavilion during the London Olympic Games in summer 2012.

He will be revealing the design plans of KREOD Trade Pavilion Rio 2016 and its visionary initiative at the Launch. He will also discuss further details about the mission, purpose, and vast number of opportunities available for KREOD’s associates and benefactors.

 

Flavio Marega

Also speaking at the event will be Flávio Marega, Minister Councillor for London’s Embassy of Brazil, and whose diplomatic career and passion for Brazilian economic and financial affairs has led to his travelling across the western world as well as the Middle East. Mr Marega has assumed a key role within many multilateral conventions and negotiating rounds, including the Negotiating group on Trade in Services of the FTAA, that was held in Panama between 2001 and 2002, and the WTO’s Ministerial Conference in Qatar in 2001. He has also participated in several trade fairs throughout his career in Bahrain and Argentina, and therefore is in an excellent position from which to comprehensively illustrate Brazil’s present economy, in addition to its prospects for growth.


Sir Peter Heap KCMG

Sir Peter’s impressive service in the British Foreign and Commonwealth Office has taken him to Europe, Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, with his final assignment being that of British Ambassador to Brazil. Upon leaving diplomatic service, he then proceeded to gain a wide breadth of commercial experience with HSBC Investment Bank, Regal Petroleum, and the Brazilian Chamber of Commerce in the UK. His knowledge and experience puts him in an ideal position to offer valuable insight into cross border investment prospects in Brazil and discuss the myriad of diverse opportunities available through the KREOD International Trade Pavilion for entrepreneurs and corporations looking to expand.

Our second THE GIFT LIVE Event will take place on July 11th, 2013 and you’re invited.



At THE GIFT LIVE, we are aboutliving the Law of Contribution  which states that, “The level of your success and happiness is in direct proportion to the number of people you serve selflessly.”


So why are we coming together to give The Gift Live?

We want you to experience the joy and benefits of living a life of contribution, a life of agenda free giving and limitless receiving. By giving and receiving The Gift you’ll see growth and acceleration in every area of your life. You have to experience it yourself!


OUR MISSION is to create a world where people naturally contribute to each other, knowing that when we are in service to others, we transform our own lives and the world around us


What people are saying from the last event...  

"Thank you for your invitation to The Gift Event last week. We had our reservations about going because we were told that every attendee were graduates from your course and have been to at least one event before; we had doubts if we would know what to do :)


Yet you and many others at the event have reminded us, that contributing is not something we practise within the confines of a classroom or an event; but rather, a way of life. And it is true, we have lived like this for a while, and you have reminded us that in order to give tirelessly, we need to give successfully, too - not at the expense of ourselves.


For these lessons and the wonderful connecting moments, you have our gratitude. We look forward to connecting with you further. Have a beautiful week ahead!"

- Val and Tay

Please join us at our 4th Annual Golf Fundraiser to raise funds for "The Safe Water Project", which develops sustainable drinking water projects in East Africa.  Enviro-Stewards will cover the cost of golf and dinner for participants (approximate value $70).  Therefore, any donations by participants will flow directly through to provision of safe water.

The tournament will be at Doon Valley Golf Course (500 Doon Valley Drive).  Similar to last year’s tournament, skill is entirely optional!

During the registration process, you'll have the option of choosing either 18 holes of golf & dinner, 9 holes of golf & dinner, or dinner only, as well as requesting club rentals or a vegetarion dinner.  Closer to the event date, we'll let you know your start time for golf.

Background

On July 9th, 2011, South Sudan became the newest country in the world when it separated from Sudan.  However, most residents do not have access to safe drinking water.  In 2007, Enviro-Stewards helped establish a locally-owned and operated BioSand Filter (BSF) construction project in Kajo Keji, South Sudan.  Funds from the 2012 golf fundraiser were used to help establish a new BSF project in Juba, the capital of South Sudan, where many residents are drinking untreated Nile River water.  These funds helped to purchase a three-wheel motorcylce and trailer necessary to deliver the completed filters (see photo below).  

Funds from this year's tournament will be used to purchase a motrocycle and trailer to deliver and re-inspect BSFs at the Kajo Keji project.  They will also help train South Sudanese to establish a BSF project in Yei, South Sudan during 2014.







Scan the QR code below with your smartphone to read more about BioSand Filters.

Save the date !!!
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dr. Yu-Lan Lin, nominated by the Massachusetts Foreign Language Association, is currently the Senior Program Director of the World Languages Program of the Boston Public Schools. She began her 33-year career as an educator at the Josiah Quincy Elementary School in Boston in 1979 as a Cantonese kindergarten bilingual teacher. Four years later, she started the Mandarin program at Snowden High School, the very first and longest-running Chinese program offered by a public school in the state of Massachusetts. In 1997, she assumed her present responsibility as the district supervisor for world languages.

Dr. Lin has been involved in numerous state and national projects and initiatives that have had a direct and profound impact on the teaching and learning of world languages. She was instrumental in the development of the National Standards of Chinese Language in the late 90’s, and has twice participated in the development and subsequent revision of the Massachusetts Foreign Language Framework. She served on the Foreign Language National Assessment of Educational Progress Committee (NAEP) and the National Board for Professional Teaching Standards in World Languages Committee (NBPTS), and co-authored the CLASS Professional Standards for K-12 Chinese Language Teachers in 2007. Most recently, she has been actively involved in the College Board’s Advanced Placement Chinese Program, serving on its Curriculum Development and Assessment Task Force and serving as its national consultant.

The spectrum of Dr. Lin’s involvement on various boards includes: Past President of the Massachusetts Foreign Language Association, Past President and current Executive Director of the Chinese Language Association of Secondary-Elementary Schools (CLASS), Board of Directors of the Northeast Conference on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (NECTFL), and Board of Directors on the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL).

Dr. Lin is a deeply committed and tireless educator who frequently presents from local to international levels on various topics related to the improvement of language education. This dedication is exemplified by a number of prestigious awards that she has received throughout her career: the 2004 MaFLA Distinguished Service Award, the 2010 NECTFL Nelson Brooks Distinguished Services and Leadership Award, and the 2010 ACTFL Florence Steiner Award for Leadership in K-12 Foreign Language Education.

Lin holds a B.A. degree in Turkish Language and Culture; an M.Ed. in Bilingual and Multicultural Studies; and an Ed.D in Reading and Language Development from Boston University.

This course is intended for students who have successfully completed Collage and Assemblage 1 and for those who wish to further explore their explorations. Students will work with a wide range of found materials which are transformed through the process of collage, assemblage and installation. This course is structured thematically, with a series of projects based on one or more topics for exploration. Some of the past investigations include fairytales, mapping and cities, and the sensory body. Students can choose to work on structured assignments or in a self-directed way with a view towards developing a cohesive body of work. Throughout the course, reference will be made to the history of collage and assemblage as well as collage and assemblage as a contemporary art practice. These references will inform and enrich art making, dialogue, and discussion.

Prerequisite: Collage and Assemblage 1 or Equivalent experience

We are a national business alliance that represents the nation's top small emerging and mid-size firms. As such, we leverage the collective voice of our member firms to influence federal policies that impact their growth and sustainability.  


MTA consists of federal contractors that represent a cross section of industries-from information technology to manufacturing to construction. These businesses service federal, state, and local governments, and employ millions of Americans across the nation. In support of these firms, MTA serves as a vehicle for business growth and development by educating member firms on business opportunities, and helping to build teaming and partnering relationships.     

 

To learn more about Mid-Tier Advocacy, visit www.midtier.org.

 

Learn about our efforts to level the playing field for small business at www.businessgrowthforall.org.

org_desc:
Mfantsipim was the first secondary school to be established in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) in 1876, and in 1905 it moved to its present location at Kwabotwe Hill in the northern part of the town, at the top of Kotokoraba Road in Cape Coast. The school sometimes has been referred to as "Kwabotwe" for that reason. It has turned out some of the country's best known public figures in all walks of life, men such as Alex Quaison-Sackey, the first black African to serve as President of the General Assembly of the United Nations, Kofi Annan, the former UN Secretary Genera. It was deemed to be a Grammar School because Latin and Greek were taught but the school also offered carpentry, art and crafts and it has generally been known as "Mfantsipim School". It was an all-boys boarding school although the intake included a small number of "day students", that is, pupils who attended school from home. Girls were later admitted to the sixth form.

Today Mfantsipm is an all-boys secondary institution. Mfantsipim is affectionately referred to as "The School" by its alums (old boys) due to the institution's historic origins.

Building Sustainable Business Models &

Why to Ask, "Can It Go On Forever?"

Each of us is a social media entrepreneur. We have Facebook, Twitter, email accounts and so much more. The proliferation of media has made our online actions profoundly affect the lives of countless colleagues, friends and loved ones.

 

As Founder and President of EcoMedia, acquired by CBS, Paul Polizzotto has successfully harnessed the power of media to better our world with the world's most recognized brands and nonprofits nationwide. Together, we will gather to hear Paul's story, ask questions, and engage in dialogue about what makes the best business models for a better planet.

 

Paul and his team have developed a broad network of partnerships with leading nonprofit organizations and city and county governments - all of which have environmental, health, or education projects in need of funding. We'll hear how EcoMedia's model makes a real, tangible impact in the communities it serves, ensuring that its projects are meaningful and generate quantifiable benefits - not only for citizens, but for its partners, as well. 

 

Paul will share tactics that apply to all new businesses, like how to ensure your business model will be sustainable. For example, Paul says one of the most important questions to ask is "Can it go on forever?" 

 

Join us as we welcome this inspiring change-maker to our fireside to ask these questions, and many more in honor of Mother Earth and how we can ensure a great future for all. Feel free to start the conversation on Twitter with @PaulPolizzotto and @GreenSpacesHome.
name: CBS EcoMedia's Paul Polizzotto on Sustainable Business Models

description:
Seminar Synopsis

  • Effective pitching is about connecting with potential clients, investors or sponsors and in doing so convincing them you are someone they can work with, best-in-class and value for money (often in that order).
  • This 1½ hour seminar will set out some basic guidelines for effective pitching, and in doing so, highlight some important questions you should be asking yourself when preparing for pitches.
  • It will run through key aspects such as: foreseeing questions, the best materials to support the pitch, who to take and how to connect in the meeting itself in order to get your message across. 

 Who should attend?

  • Both experienced presenters wishing to refresh their skills and those just starting out having to sell themselves or their company and what they have to offer. 
  • These guidelines apply equally to professional services organisations, media and creative industries and entrepreneurs. 
  • The focus will be on scenarios where you already have secured a meeting or you are in competitive tender, but the broad themes will be valid for any situation where you are looking to sell yourself.

 Who’s running it?

  • Alistair Seaton has 15 years of experience of presenting complex views to diverse audiences via presentations, workshops, conferences, articles and written-reports. 
  • Alistair has worked with a wide range of clients, including designers, lawyers and architects.
  • Prior to setting up his consultancy, he was head of the European strategy team of a global investment manager, where he was involved in all aspects of new business generation and regularly pitched for, and won, new clients.

 Other information

  • The seminar will run from 5:30 pm to 7:00 pm in the Mercury Room. Registration and tea, coffee & cookies from 5:15 pm.
name: Connect, Connect, Connect: How to Pitch Effectively and Win New Business

The Seattle Seahawks will open 14 training camp practices at the Virginia Mason Athletic Center (VMAC) in Renton beginning Thursday, July 25th and concluding Wednesday, August 14th.

Fans interested in attending Training Camp presented by Bing may register, beginning on Thursday, June 27th. Exclusive presales will begin for Season Ticket Holders on June 24th and for Blue Pride Members on June 26th.

Registration will be available on a first-come, first-served basis, exclusively through this website, and there is a maximum of six registrants per group. Fans 15 years or younger must be accompanied by an adult. Only fans that register through this site will be allowed to attend practice.

A $7 transportation fee will be charged per person, as fans will be required to park offsite at The Landing in Renton and ride a shuttle to the VMAC before and after each practice. The VMAC parking lot will be closed to the public.

Guests will receive transportation transfers and training camp passes upon checking in at the Seahawks Training Camp Guest Services location at The Landing, located near the parking garage and movie theater at the shopping center.

More information:

  • Camp Guidelines
  • Transportation
  • What to do in Renton
  • Contact
  • Cancellation Policy

Cancellations

In the event that practice is cancelled or moved indoors, fans will be asked to depart the VMAC facility. We will attempt to notify all registrants of such cancellations 24 hours in advance via automated phone message, text message and/or email. Fan's following the team's official Facebook and Twitter accounts will also be notified of cancellations if necessary.

Raincheck dates are available as necessary and will be announced for select sessions that are cancelled or moved indoors. Practices are subject to change without notice.

Speakers:

 

Chris Boys - Export Consultant, Katabolt

Business Stream: A guide to locating overseas revenue streams in 4 sprints.
 

Export consultancy Katabolt helps entrepreneurs, start-ups and established businesses to fast track the export process into foreign markets whilst minimising the costs and resources typically involved.  Katabolt is based in Auckland, helping New Zealand companies build their export capability to develop and execute market entry strategies. Clients benefit from Katabolt’s on-the-ground contacts in 26 countries to accelerate the path-to-market process.

Christopher Boys is the driving force behind Katabolt, with over 20 years of sales experience across a number of industries including 15 years in the technology sector both in New Zealand and abroad and three years in the education sector.  He also has intrinsic knowledge of the manufacturing and food and beverage industries.

Where are your first, second, third steps export-wise? 

Katabolt sees many companies take an approach of Fire-Fire-Fire and hope they land the right channels and revenue streams.  In 2013 it’s all about executing Market Opportunity Assessment (MOA) before you spend any investment on Google AdWords, remarketing or traditional media. 

The Katabolt team are excited and delighted to talk about tips to gaining measureable revenue streams in 2 months.
   
 

Bry Ashman - Lead Developer, Trineo

Technical Stream:  How Trineo are using Amazon Web Services (AWS) and AWS Summit Overview

Trineo are experts in Salesforce.com, Force.com and custom Ruby on Rails software development with offices in Christchurch, Auckland and Sydney.

Bry Ashman is Lead Developer in the Trineo Bespoke Solutions team. He has built a number of applications over recent years that utilise components from AWS including EC2, S3, Elastic Map Reduce, Redshift and Dynamo.

Bry will be providing an overview of the AWS platform and highlights from the recent AWS Summit in Auckland.
   
 

Lee Butts - Head of Development, MahiFX

Technical Stream: How MahiFX are using AWS throughout the Development process 

MahiFX provides a proprietary-built FX trading platform that provides retail traders with direct access to institutional quality execution speeds and spreads.

Lee Butts has over 12 years of software development experience since graduating from Canterbury University with an honours degree in Computer Science.  His background is in Java and JVM based development and has contributed to several open source projects over the years. He has worked in a wide range of industries, most recently in financial services and advertising.  He returned home to Christchurch in 2010, having lived and worked in Australia for 8 years and now heads up the Christchurch development team of MahiFX.

Lee will speak about how MahiFX use Amazon AWS in most aspects of their development process including design, build and testing to achieve quickest time to market for new features while controlling costs.

description:
Join international teachers Jai Kartar and BenJahmin on a unique and wonderful journey in the pure natural setting of the Austrian countryside. There you will plant deep roots into your essential being practising Kundalini yoga, Shakti Dance and The Deepening work (created by Jai Kartar, this uses dance, music, meditations, Tantra and constellations to create a unique experience of self). 


BenJahmin and Jai will take you on a journey of falling in love with the feminine, with the masculine, with your inner child as the adult - and with the presence within us all.


Through this unique fusion of dance, meditation and other deep practises you will experience an appreciation of your true self.


Union from the roots will embed a sense of peace and belonging which will stay with you well beyond the retreat. 


 

What you will enjoy

There are two classes each day: one taught by Benjamin and the other by Jai. Some classes are held inside and others outside in the natural surroundings. There is also optional early morning Kundalini practise.

Here's how a day at the retreat will flow:

 5am   Kundalini yoga practise (optional)
 8.30am  Breakfast
 10am - 12.30pm  Workshop 
 1.30pm  Lunch
 4 - 6.30pm   Workshop
 7.30pm  Dinner

 
In the evenings we will have special events, live music by Jai and BenJahmin, ceremony and chillout / free time. There will be plenty of space to allow the workshop material to sink in.


About the accommodation

You can choose to stay in a beautiful guest house nearby, or in the house of our Austrian hosts (limited spots available).


About the food


Enjoy three vegetarian meals a day lovingly prepared by Bayari Beegan, who specialises in nourishing, revitalising dishes. She will use locally grown vegetables. 

You will be invited to the kitchen to help with the preparation of meals at some point in the retreat. This will be a bonding communal experience and lots of fun!

We will also ask for help with serving and clearing up, to ensure everyone in the group opens to the element of Seva (selfless service).

 

 

About the costs

Here are the costs which includes all teaching, three wonderful vegetarian meals per day and accommodation in local guesthouses or in our hosts' home.


Guesthouse accommodation

Deposit: £300 / 350 Euros (please pay this non-refundable amount now to secure your spot)

Full amount: £750 / 865 Euros

 

Dormitory accommodation

Deposit: £175/ 200 Euros (please pay this non-refundable amount now to secure your spot)

Full amount: £575/ 665 Euros


About the location

The retreat is held in a beautiful village called Ybbsitz in the countryside of Austria which has hills, waterfalls and pure clean air. Here are a couple of images of where we will be:

Secluded retreat venue


Private roof garden


How to get there

You can fly to Linz via Frankfurt. Or you can fly to Salzburg or Vienna and then taking a train to Linz. From there you can either take a train or a taxi on to Ybbsitz. If you would like more information about this, please let us know.

If you are driving you can easily get there from Czech, Italy, Germany, Hungary.

 

About the theme of the retreat: union of the roots

Our natural essence is this love
We find it first through the feminine through the mother
Somehow all of us must bow to that within us and outside of us to come from the old paradigm to a new way
We see it in how the world treats the environment, how we love our mothers, other women, how much we engage with self love from the feeling of self care...
It is time to remember our roots
To allow them to be with us
In presence, all is healed 

In understanding we are all presence and yet our journey to remembering and embodying presence is through union...

Union of child adult 
Union of masculine and feminine
Union of the sacred and forbidden
They include each other but the self enquiry and experience is different

You will learn techniques and explore many deepening practices but more than this you will have an experience of a deepening within you, without spiritual jargon or dogma. Using flow and structure we can find our way to be our unique sound of presence.

Then we can look at a deeper contact with masculine, the new territory. What is the quest?
What is it to truly be a man or embody a masculine part that is embracing the new way? What does that look like? What does that feel like? Does he have to be a warrior in every moment?
Can he put down his armour and hold that cup of love for all to see and feel?
He needs deep love of his own feminine for this, in a healthy way


This is a journey to fall in love with the feminine, with the masculine and with the child and adult that is presence within US! You will learn techniques, explore many deepening practices but more than this you can have an experience of a deepening within you, without spiritual jargon or dogma. Using flow and structure we can find our way to be our unique sound of presence.
name: Union from the Roots Retreat - Austria
org_desc: Both BenJahmin and Jai Kartar are teachers, facilitators and recording artists from the UK. Friends and colleagues, they are usually working on solo projects and music, however their expansion into working with the sacred feminine has brought them together for this retreat, to share their experience and friendship offering a wholeness and sweetness to the event.

description:
FILM FESTIVALS 101: “MY BUDDY WENT TO CANNES AND ALL I GOT WAS THIS LOUSY T-SHIRT”

So you submit your film to Sundance, it wins the grand jury prize, and you become a famous director. Not! On the other hand, don’t be a playa-hater. You don’t have to be an insider at CAA to showcase your film at a prestige venue.

Even with the advent of YouTube and other distribution platforms, film festivals can raise your directorial profile dramatically, lead to career-making opportunities, or at least provide nice vacations in Europe.

This four-hour seminar covers these topics and more:

  • Determining your goals for screening at festivals.
  • Assembling a realistic list of target festivals.
  • How to build relationships with festival programmers without looking like a stalker.
  • How to make your film festival application stand out from other applications.
  • How to maximize audience exposure to your film at a festival and how to leverage it.
  • PR: Before, during, and after a festival.
  • How to network at festivals.
  • Budgeting: before and during exhibition on the festival circuit.
  • Leveraging exhibition by one festival to get into other festivals.
  • Pet peeves of programmers that may result in instant rejection of your film.
  • Online vs. DVD submissions: Do they matter?
  • The impact of production value and stylization in programming decisions.
  • The limitations of the festival circuit. How far can you go?
  • Film Festival Etiquette: You and your film will come and go, the festival staff will not.
  • Nepotism: myth and reality. 

NOTE: I am a programmer at a prestige festival. However, attending this seminar in no way gives you favored access to myself or other programmers. In fact, I probably will recuse myself if I am asked to evaluate your film in an official capacity. This seminar is no way associated with Slamdance or any other festival. I provide the seminar for informational purposes only. 

About The Instructor: 

Noel Lawrence curates, distributes, and writes about cinema. He has founded and guided film ventures in home video, online media, and festival environments. Combining a grad-school background with over a decade of experience in the entertainment industry, Lawrence specializes in promoting obscure and innovative films in ways that attract mainstream audiences and build distinct cinematic “brands” in a highly competitive media marketplace.

With Burke Roberts, he oversees the programming of the "Anarchy" section at the Slamdance Film Festival in Park City, Utah. As a filmmaker, he previously has exhibited work at festivals such as  IFF Rotterdam, Thessaloniki International Film Festival, Slamdance, Cork Film Festival, Nashville Film Festival and Ann Arbor.
name: Film Festivals 101

Holbein's Danse Macabre from Wikimedia

 

Walk Macabre: Dispatching the dead in Smithfield and Finsbury

During “Walk Macabre”, Jiff Bayliss explores some of London’s most ghoulish last resting places. Robert Bard, author of “Graveyard London” commented that “many hundreds of generations of Londoners lie beneath the City feet without us knowing”; this walk suggests they were the lucky ones.

Starting at the site of Newgate Prison and continuing through Smithfield to Bunhill cemetery, it explores executions, pestilence and lost burial grounds. Aimed at a general audience and those with an interest in history’s darker side, see where many Londoners met a literally sticky end. After the walk, you’ll wonder whether every open plot in central London was once someone’s graveyard.

Meets outside the Caffe Nero shop just outside exit 2 of St Paul's UndergrounD station - look for the man in the Stove Pipe hat.  You can check travel options at the Transport for London Journey Planner.
name: Walk Macabre - dispatching the dead in Smithfield and Finsbury

Considéré aujourd’hui comme l’un des festivals les plus importants du pays, le festival Timitar nous offre chaque année une manifestation, désormais bien enracinée, il œuvre activement à la promotion des cultures régionales du Souss Massa Drâa : il a ainsi su donner à la créativité amazighe ses lettres de noblesse.

Mais le Festival Timitar est avant tout une fête ouverte à tous.
Une fête où les musiques amazighes et les musiques du monde se rassemblent dans une même volonté d’échange, de partage.
Fédérateur de projets de développement régional, Timitar favorise également la créativité des artistes locaux. Il est donc une illustration vivante, chaque fois renouvelée, de cette aptitude qu’a la musique à rassembler et à faire dialoguer les différences qui peuvent exister entre les peuples, mais également entre les hommes.
Le Festival Timitar est devenu ainsi un rendez-vous incontournable dans le paysage culturel marocain.
En quatre éditions, le Festival Timitar est parvenu à fidéliser un public de plus en plus nombreux. Animés par une curiosité et un enthousiasme grandissant, les spectateurs peuvent y découvrir, ou y redécouvrir, les trésors musicaux d’ici et d’ailleurs ; son impact dépasse dorénavant largement les limites géographiques de la région Souss Massa Drâa et du Maroc.
Pour cette dixième édition, près d’une quarantaine de groupes d’origines très variées se produiront sur scène. Qu’il soit originaire de l’ensemble du territoire marocain, de diverses contrées du monde ou issu de l’émigration amazighe, chaque artiste enrichira ce programme.
En outre, l’édition 2013 du Festival mettra aussi l’accent sur les différents styles des musiques actuelles, notamment, le rock fusion, le Hip-hop, le Deejaying et les musiques électroniques seront aussi à l’honneur.
Le public qui se donne rendez-vous chaque année à Agadir est indifféremment constitué de jeunes et d’adultes, venant seuls, en famille ou en groupe et issu de toutes origines culturelles et de toutes conditions sociales et de zones géographiques très variées (public local, régional, national et international).
Les spectateurs de Timitar se verront offrir, une fois de plus un festival dont la richesse, la nouveauté et l’extrême diversité sauront les enthousiasmer et les surprendre.
... Plus de détail sur www.festivaltimitar.ma

BACKGROUND

Over the years and more recently with the redevelopment of Warmun Community, it has been noted that there is a significant need for the provision of Gija Cultural Education Training. This training provides the necessary information, skills and capacity for organisations and individuals providing services or doing business in Warmun and its surrounding outstations (Crocodile Hole, Bow River, Norton Bore, Violet Valley, Frog Hollow, Osmond Valley and Dolly Hole).

In March 2011, after the flood and in consultation with Gija elders, the Gija Cultural Education Training Program was designed to address the needs identified through the rebuild of Warmun Community and the reintroduction of community members alongside contractors and service providers.

This program is vital to establishing Warmun as a vibrant, healthy Community.

 

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

Over the past two weeks, service providers visiting or living in Warmun Community have been asked for their valuable feedback via an online survey. We now have these results and have used your input as the foundation for creating a suitable Gija Cultural Education Training program.

The Gija Cultural Education Training program has been designed by Gija people and endorsed by Gija elders for delivery. On behalf of the people of Warmun Community, we thank you for your time to complete and co-design this program.

PROGRAM OUTLINE

The Gija Cultural Education Training Program is a day long (9am-4pm) course, delivered on country in Warmun Community with visits to particular sites of importance to Gija people. The program will include the following with morning tea, lunch and afternoon tea breaks:

  • Welcome to Country (performed by Gija women)
  • Gija Country and Customs
  • Archaeological heritage
  • Ethnographical heritage (site visit)
  • Pre and Post Colonisation, Policies and Legislation
  • Impact of Policies and Legislation
  • Gija social structures
  • What is Cultural Respect
  • Access to Country 
  • Importance of Country
  • Gija Kinships
  • Gija Dreaming Stories (site visit)
  • Close

FAQs

Who will be delivering the course?
The course will be delivered by Kia Dowell, co-founder of The Cultural Connection Code. As a Gija woman with extensive community and commercial knowledge, Kia will provide training in a culturally appropriate way and provide insights into both traditional and contemporary topics. 

Learn more about The Cultural Connection Code here

Connect with The Cultural Connection Code today

Are there ID requirements or an age limit to enter the event?
We ask that all participants present valid photo identification at registration.

 

What are my transport/parking options getting to the event?
There is ample on-site parking and a map of the Community with directions will be provided to participants prior to their selected training course. 

 

What can/can't I bring to the event?
Course participants will be walking in and around Warmun Community, we ask that you please bring a hat, closed in shoes and a water bottle. Although there is a clinic in the Community in case of emergencies, if you are taking any medication please ensure you bring this with you.

 

Where can I contact the organizer with any questions?
For more information please email connect@theculturalconnectioncode.com 

 

What is the refund policy?
In the event that you cannot attend the training and notice has been received within 72 hours a full refund will be made available.

 

See how technology is bringing Gija culture into the 21st century

_
name: Gija Cultural Education Training
org_desc:
Warmun Community (also known as Turkey Creek) and Warmun are a township and locality in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, located on the Great Northern Highway, 3009 km northeast of Perth.[2] The closest populated town is Halls Creek.

The area was settled by European pastoralists in the 19th century but the community was established in 1901 when the state government built a ration depot at Turkey Creek.[3]

The Ngalangangpum School was established in town at the request of the community. Built in 1979 the school allowed students to stay in town rather than attend St Josephs school in Wyndham and only come home over the holidays. The school was significantly upgraded in 1987, then again in 1990 so secondary schooling could occur in town and upgraded again in 2001[4]

Course Description:

This seminar was designed collaboratively to provide rehabilitation professionals with an increased understanding of ethics and jurisprudence and the relevance ethics play in everyday therapeutic environments. Special focus will include the role of the business aspects of ethics especially with the changing view of healthcare and specialized areas including end of life and informed consent. Throughout the seminar, the Code of Ethics specific to the rehabilitation disciplines will be referenced and applied to case examples across treatment populations and the health care continuum.


Course Objectives:

By the end of the course, participants will be able to:

  • Describe the key elements of ethics and laws that govern rehabilitation professionals
  • Apply ethical concepts to commonly identified situations in rehabilitation practice
  • Demonstrate the ability to analyze and interpret situations to determine if an ethical dilemma exists
  • Decrease potential at risk behavior through analysis of ethical dilemmas and utilize ethical clinical decision making to make recommendations that are defensible with the Code of Ethics of PT, OT and/or Speech Therapy


Course Relevance:

The course was specifically designed for rehabilitation professionals, including physical therapists and assistants in regards to Ethical decision making and legal systems governing the practice of Physical Therapy. The course will enhance the participants understanding of Ethics and Jurisprudence as it relates to everyday practice and broaden knowledge bases related to health care business ethics, end of life issues and informed consent.


Course Schedule:

Registration begins half hour prior to start time. There is one 15 minute break.

Speakers:

Dan W. BaileyDan W. Bailey is the Executive Director of Wildland Fire, Natural Resource, Environmental and Natural Hazard Programs for the International Code Council™, based in Washington, D.C. Bailey’s background includes serving as a staff assistant to Oregon U.S. Senator Wayne Morse, then moving into the federal government where he served as a professional Foresters and Supervisory Forester involved with land management, forestry and wildland fire programs for more than 30 years, with assignments in Oregon, Idaho, Montana, Arizona and Washington, DC. He held numerous positions including serving as the National Program Manager for the USDA Forest Service Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) Fire and Firewise programs, prior to retiring from the agency in 2004. Bailey was the co-founder of the National Firewise Communities Workshop series, a highly successful national campaign dealing with building in the wildland/urban interface that trained over 10,000 individuals in hundreds of communities throughout the U.S. While with the USDA Forest Service, Bailey served as a National Incident Commander of one of the National Incident Management Teams and led the efforts on more than 200 of the nation’s largest and most destructive wildfires, as well as dealing with hurricanes and other national disasters.

Mel CosgroveMel Cosgrove is a senior member of the ICC government relation team. He is a graduate of the University of South Alabama and retired from Mobile Fire Department. While employed by MFD he served as chairman of the Southeastern Association of Fire Chiefs Code Committee and served on the code development committee of the Southern Building Code Congress. He also served on the drafting committee of the International Fire Code.

Coleen VanzantColeen has worked with the Alabama Forestry Commission for 27 years, most of that time being spent in Public Information and Education. This includes serving 7 years as Public Information Manager for the agency. In 2009 she moved to the Operations Division of the AFC to serve as Wildland Urban Interface Coordinator for North Alabama as well as the state coordinator for Firewise Communities/USA.

She is an alumnus of Samford University in Birmingham where she received a Bachelor of Science Degree in Paralegal Science and Wallace State College at Hanceville where she earned an Associate’s Degree in Liberal Arts. She completed the Alabama Forestry Commission Ranger Academy in 1988.

Coleen lives at Hanceville in Cullman County on a farm that has been in her family for six generations. She is an active member of Bethlehem East Baptist Church.

Mission Statement

Global Empowerment Theatre is an educational theatre organization developed to empower people around the world using playwriting and theatrical techniques. We believe that using theatre maximizes student learning by building confidence, empowering students, and providing a creative outlet within a structured learning environment. We work with people who have limited educational resources and for whom English literacy is key to future educational and community success.


Background/History

Since 2006, Jennifer Holmes and John Socas have traveled to Zanzibar in East Africa, using theatre to improve English language literacy, foster critical thinking skills, explore creative self-expression, and develop a sense of world citizenship. In 2010, Maya Turner Singh and Ashley Olson joined as members of the core GETheatre team, bringing with them the vision of expansion.

In January of 2010 GETheatre began a pilot program in Bangalore, India with The Parikrma Humanity Foundation (a non-profit school for slum children and orphans).  Since then GETheatre’s partnership with Parikrma has grown into annual programming with two classes of students each January and comprehensive training with Parikrma’s teachers to integrate drama into their classrooms.
